note.summary: PathUtils.is_passable must return false for out-of-bounds tiles; treating them as passable lets BFS/pathfinding escape the room grid and hang room generation and targeting.

RunEngine, CombatEngine, RoomGenerator, and ProgressionStore own all gameplay rules in pure RefCounted scripts over dictionaries so the same codepath powers both the playable scenes and headless regression tests.
UI validation relies on screenshot probes for the menu, room start, combat, and post-card states so layout changes can be judged visually even in headless-first sessions.
Traversal stays on the room board: route choices come from clicking highlighted door tiles in room mode, while the minimap remains non-interactive and only provides orientation/context.
UI copy should stay terse and action-oriented; prefer visual communication, concise labels, and lightweight overlays over explanatory panel text or multi-sentence instructions.

RunScene builds the camp-menu and pile-inspector overlays in code; resume vs. new-run flow is chosen from the root meta key 'labyrinth_resume_saved_run' and backed by ProgressionStore's separate saved-run slot.

UI regressions should be checked with screenshot probes for combat, targeting, after-play, the camp menu, and pile inspectors, because key overlays are built in code and scene-instantiation tests alone will miss visual breakage.
The project theme must reference fonts/PressStart2P-Regular.tres, not the raw .ttf; Godot's custom project theme loading fails to resolve the .ttf as a FontFile in headless/tests.

RunScene sizes MiniMapOverlay in _layout_mini_map_overlay() from the current viewport instead of fixed offsets because a larger static corner map was overflowing smaller windows and obscuring the board.

Pixel-font cards need a tall card ratio and clipped contents; near-square hand/modal cards cause the title, art, and footer to spill, so the shared CardWidget is tuned around concise action summaries and roughly 1.4x height-to-width sizing.

Combat hands are only dead when both the printed card previews and the drag fallback previews are invalid; Pass logic and hand dimming need to account for the alternate 2-attack and 2-move plays, not just the printed card text.

Block behavior is codified in regression tests: player block must absorb damage across the whole enemy phase, and enemy block must persist into the next player turn until it is spent by incoming damage or cleared when that enemy acts again.

Combat hands are only dead when both the printed card previews and the drag fallback previews are invalid; Pass logic and hand dimming need to account for the alternate 2-attack and 2-move plays, not just the printed card text.

UI regressions need screenshot probes for combat, pile inspectors, the drag overlay, fallback targeting, and after-play states because those overlays are built in code and scene-instantiation tests miss layout and input breakage.

Multi-action cards treat targeted steps as skippable by default unless an action is marked required; the preview auto-skips dead target steps and the combat choice bar exposes Skip for optional follow-ups that still have valid targets.

Enemy block is preview-time: assigning a revealed intent preloads any block onto the enemy for the current player turn, then enemy phase clears that preview block before actions resolve so it does not carry into the next turn.

Regression tests now lock the updated combat rules: revealed enemy block must mitigate the current player turn immediately, and multi-action cards must stay playable when optional targeted steps can be skipped or auto-skipped.

Targetless cards must commit on the initial click path itself; previewing their resolved state without immediately awaiting _play_player_card leaves a ghost preview that cancels on the next selection instead of spending the card.
Hand-card damage text should come from CombatEngine final-damage and modifier helpers, using a preview-state copy so Ember Lens stays aligned with live combat on multi-action cards.
UI probes must clear saved runs and load a fresh deterministic run state before capturing; otherwise screenshots can silently reuse stale progress and mask changes like enemy-density or HUD updates.

note.details: The UI probe does not move the real mouse, so drag-overlay screenshots can miss the dragged card unless the probe calls _update_drag_proxy_position before capture. Keep doing that when visually verifying drag-and-drop regressions.
note.summary: Drag-overlay probes must place the drag proxy explicitly

note.details: The dynamic draw/discard/burn widgets still sit on top of the original scene controls, so _build_pile_widget should zero out those legacy children. Empty-pile captions also need to stay short (DECK/DISC/BURN); letting discard render DISCARD can overflow and look like a stretched pile even when the frame is fine.
note.summary: Pile widgets need collapsed legacy children and short empty captions

note.details: The hand ScrollContainer should use an empty panel style and clip_contents=false. Otherwise hovered cards get their tops cut off and the hand row can show a darker panel strip that reads like a mismatched background behind the cards.
note.summary: Hover-lifted cards need unclipped transparent hand scroll

note.details: The dragged card proxy should be top_level and the source hand widget should be hidden instead of rebuilding the whole hand at drag start. Rebuilding under the cursor or leaving the source visible causes jittery drag behavior and visual fighting between the proxy and the hand layout.
note.summary: Stable card drag needs a top-level proxy and hidden source card

note.details: The dragged card proxy should be top_level and the source hand widget should be hidden instead of rebuilding the whole hand at drag start. Rebuilding under the cursor or leaving the source visible causes jittery drag behavior and visual fighting between the proxy and the hand layout.
note.summary: Stable card drag needs a top-level proxy and hidden source card

note.details: CardWidget's hover/selection pose adjusts position.y, which is fine inside the hand layout but breaks top_level drag proxies by snapping them toward y=0. For drag proxies, keep absolute position untouched and only apply safe visual properties like scale.
note.summary: Top-level card proxies must not reuse position-based hover lift
Elemental combat stores burn, freeze, shock, poison, and stoneskin directly on unit dictionaries so cards, room-tuned enemy intents, board badges, and tests all share one status model.

Enemy threat previews follow the hovered enemy's current intent, keep move_toward/move_away directional, and exclude move tiles from attack tiles so blue movement and red threat overlays stay distinct.

Player freeze and shock badges need to merge player_turn_restrictions with the stored status counters, because prepare_next_player_turn consumes those counters before the board renders the locked turn.
Enemy attack steps now enqueue only when the player state actually changes, and shallow elemental rooms tone down enemy status payloads so freeze/shock pressure ramps up later in the run.
Ice and lightning enemy CC now comes only from rarer intents (weight 2 or less) at depth 3+, and those freeze/shock attacks cap their range at 4 so elemental control pressure ramps more gently.

ActionIconLibrary is the shared source of truth for reusable combat keyword icon tokens, paths, and tooltips; card summaries and combat board intents/status badges should consume its token rows instead of hand-building keyword strings.

note.details: Combat hand cards normally max at 160px wide, so treating 160px as compact makes the icon summary rows render small. The rarity footer is hidden to reserve vertical space for larger icon rows.
note.summary: Keep CardWidget compact cutoff below normal hand width

note.details: Cards and custom-drawn combat board regions should route keyword and modifier tooltip text through UiTooltipPanel so tooltip styling stays consistent and avoids the default translucent black engine tooltip.
note.summary: Use UiTooltipPanel for custom tooltip overlays

note.details: CombatBoardView draws floor/overlays first, then interleaves terrain props and unit bodies in tile draw order. Unit HUDs stay in a final pass for readability. Tall blockers (wall/pillar) tint translucent only when their prop rect overlaps a unit on a farther-back tile, using the same tile comparator as rendering.
note.summary: Depth-sort board bodies and fade foreground blockers
The reaver idle sheet is exported column-major (top-to-bottom, then left-to-right), so CombatBoardView must reorder frames instead of using the default row-major atlas order.

reason: Atlas analysis and in-engine playback verification showed the smoothest 8-frame idle loop is standard row-major order.

note.summary: The reaver idle sheet should be read in standard row-major order (left-to-right, then top-to-bottom); reordering it column-major makes the idle loop visibly less smooth.
CombatBoardView overrides the final frame of player_reaver_idle with the penultimate frame because the exported last pose makes the sword pop abruptly in motion.
CombatBoardView plays player_reaver_idle as a ping-pong loop (0..7..1) so the idle bob reverses cleanly instead of snapping from the last pose back to the first.

reason: Ping-pong looping did not improve the perceived hitch enough to keep, so CombatBoardView was reverted to the straightforward forward row-major idle loop.

note.summary: Enemy intent popups reserve a title line for the intent name, including name-only intents like Wait, so layout code and tests should size popups from total intent lines instead of raw action-row count.

Per-enemy sprite sizing is driven by enemy_def art_scale and applied after fitting the texture, scaling around the fitted rect center so smaller variants stay tile-centered and keep their HUD alignment.
Enemy art_scale is applied after fitting, anchored at the fitted rect bottom-center so smaller sprites stay centered horizontally, keep their feet planted, and keep HUD placement stable.
Enemy intent popups now auto-expand to fit their title and token rows, preserving a fixed minimum width while preventing long names like Skitter Strike from clipping.
CombatBoardView auto-loads same-stem _idle sheets into 4x2 frame loops and only uses those frames when a unit is not currently being moved or focused by combat presentation.
Move and attack targeting now rely on tile highlights and path lines only; CombatBoardView no longer draws extra preview glyphs like circles or plus signs over target tiles.
Auto room dialogue is keyed by room coord plus turns_spent so _refresh_ui() can safely rerun without reopening the overlay, while revisiting the same room later still retriggers the conversation.

RunEngine traversal is now a sealed ring graph: non-center rooms keep east/west same-depth links, only one quarter of each ring links deeper, and move filtering permanently blocks any room once you leave it or any exit toward lower depth.

RunEngine traversal now uses square Chebyshev rings with 8*d rooms per depth, cardinal-only perimeter links, 1/4 of each ring linking outward, inward moves locked after advancing, and empty treasure rooms falling back to room mode.

note.details: Introduced for the cinder Acolyte PNG alignment and covered by _test_enemy_art_offset_shifts_sprite_vertically in tests/run_tests.gd.
note.summary: Combat board unit art now honors per-definition art_offset_x/y after fit/scale; adjust sprite centering in enemy/npc data instead of changing global anchoring.

note.details: Default behavior stays 4x2 row-major, but cinder Acolyte uses 2x4 column_major and is covered by _test_acolyte_idle_sheet_honors_column_major_layout in tests/run_tests.gd.
note.summary: CombatBoardView idle sheets are now data-driven per unit: definitions can override idle_sheet_columns, idle_sheet_rows, and idle_sheet_order while same-stem _idle loading remains automatic.

note.details: Default behavior stays 4x2 row-major at 0.10s per frame, but cinder Acolyte uses 2x4 column_major at 0.20s per frame; covered by _test_acolyte_idle_sheet_honors_column_major_layout and _test_acolyte_idle_speed_override in tests/run_tests.gd.
note.summary: CombatBoardView idle animation is fully data-driven per unit: definitions can override idle_sheet_columns, idle_sheet_rows, idle_sheet_order, and idle_frame_seconds while same-stem _idle loading remains automatic.

note.details: This prevents enemies from spawning or walking onto exit doors and is covered by _test_room_generation_blocks_door_tiles in tests/run_tests.gd.
note.summary: Door tiles are blocking terrain for PathUtils, so movement, spawns, threat ranges, and pathfinding all treat room exits like walls.

note.details: CombatBoardView scores small sideways/upward nudges against reserved HUD rects, then falls back to a dynamic escape offset based on the stack bounds for dense overlaps; covered by _test_enemy_hud_layout_stays_centered_when_clear and _test_enemy_hud_layout_offsets_away_from_reserved_ui in tests/run_tests.gd.
note.summary: Enemy HUD collision avoidance moves the full enemy health-plus-intent stack together and draws a tether line when displaced, so overlap fixes still preserve which unit the intent belongs to.

note.details: CombatBoardView auto-loads %s_idle from the art_path basename for both enemies and NPCs. Pointing the Emaciated Man at acolyte.svg pulled in acolyte_idle.png and caused flickering; emaciated_man.svg is intentionally a unique basename with no idle companion.
note.summary: NPC combat art basenames can inherit idle sheets by stem, so static placeholder NPCs need a unique art filename with no matching *_idle texture.

note.details: Room layouts still stamp door blockers into the grid for topology/pathing, but the board renderer shows a wall unless the tile is an active exit or a sealed previously visited door from run_scene locked_door_tiles. Moving units also derive draw order from unit_world_positions so enemy move tweens do not pop back at the end.
note.summary: Combat board door visibility is presentation-driven, not layout-driven.

note.details: RunScene now pads auto-skipped and manually skipped targeted actions with INVALID_TARGET_TILE so animation playback stays aligned with the original action list, which enables one-click move-then-attack enemy shortcuts without misassigning later targets.
note.summary: Multi-action card resolution keeps a target slot per targeted step, using INVALID_TARGET placeholders for skipped steps.

note.details: run_scene now injects active_door_tiles for connected exits that should still look like doors during combat, locked_door_tiles for sealed traversal doors, and unit_draw_tiles for animated movers so CombatBoardView can keep smooth world-position interpolation without nearest-tile snapping.
note.summary: Combat board door visibility and move layering are presentation-driven via explicit door and draw-tile maps.

note.details: The HP readout is drawn inside a 12px bar with a 1px four-direction outline; bottom-anchoring the baseline at rect.size.y - 1 keeps the numerals visually centered and avoids the top-edge clipping that shows up with this pixel font.
note.summary: Health bar HP text should use a 1px bottom inset instead of the old fixed +10 baseline, or the outlined Press Start 2P digits clip against the top border.

note.details: CombatBoardView bottom-anchors both bars to the same HUD clearance, so enlarging the enemy bar grows it upward into free space without pushing it down into sprite art or breaking intent stacking.
note.summary: Enemy health bars intentionally use a larger 84x14 rect while player bars stay 78x12, because the outlined HP digits still feel cramped in a 12px enemy bar.

note.details: Voluntary player move previews and move resolution share path_for_player_action, so the previewed route matches the actual step-by-step trap triggers. Enemies treat trap tiles as blocked for intent previews and voluntary movement, but forced movement can still push or pull units through traps and trigger them immediately.
note.summary: Trap movement paths now minimize trap crossings before distance, and trap-applied freeze/shock/stun on players are deferred through pending_player_trap_restriction so they hit the next possible action after the current card resolves.

move_to_room must refresh its local rooms snapshot after _reveal_neighbors before non-combat room branches mutate room state, or treasure/campfire/NPC transitions can overwrite newly revealed exits and strand the run in a false dead end.

note.details: The balance target is acolyte average toward-move 1.0 and warden average toward-move 1.5, both still below crawler's 1.75. tests/run_tests.gd locks this pacing so these archetypes stop corner camping without becoming rushdown enemies.
note.summary: Acolytes now drift forward on every intent and wardens step forward even on Bulwark turns so low-mobility enemies keep closing space without matching crawler speed.

note.details: tests/run_tests.gd now checks per-intent movement variety plus simple per-intent averages, while still guarding that wardens remain slower than crawlers in weighted intent frequency.
note.summary: Low-mobility enemy movement is now varied by intent: acolyte steps 2/1/3 for a two-tile average, while warden steps 1/0/2 for a one-tile average.

note.details: tests/run_tests.gd checks crawler/acolyte/warden per-intent movement averages and weighted ordering so the crawler stays the fastest pressure enemy without matching the larger enemies' damage ceiling.
note.summary: Crawler intent pacing now leads the roster at 3/2/4 movement with slightly lighter 3/5 melee damage, while acolyte and warden stay at 2 and 1 average movement respectively.

note.details: CombatBoardView loads res://assets/placeholders/tiles/base_floor_tile_01..07.png, trims each texture to its used rect, precomputes a _floor_variant_by_tile lookup in set_combat_state, and falls back to the first variant when indexing misses.
note.summary: cinder floor rendering now uses seven extracted PNG variants chosen deterministically per room coordinate, with left/up neighbor de-clumping to avoid obvious repeats.

note.details: The first extraction pass kept surrounding source context inside the diamond, which could make a variant look peeled or skewed in-game. The corrected assets flood-fill the selected tile component from base_floor_tiles.png, keep neighboring tiles transparent, and CombatBoardView now loads the variant textures without trim_texture_to_used_rect.
note.summary: cinder floor variants are extracted as isolated tile-only PNGs and loaded untrimmed so every stone keeps the same isometric canvas and avoids neighbor-fragment warping.

note.details: RoomGenerator applies moss after template stamping using a room-seeded coordinate hash plus light neighbor de-clumping, keeps entry tiles cinder for readability, and never emits ember floor tiles from generation.
note.summary: Room floors now generate as cinder with deterministic moss accents, while _base_grid still consumes one legacy floor-theme roll so template and encounter RNG stay aligned with prior room seeds.

note.details: AGENTS.md tells future sessions to consult the heuristic when creating or modifying cards and to update both the doc and tool whenever combat pacing, status behavior, room spacing, enemy assumptions, fatigue, or action keywords change.
note.summary: Card balance work now uses spec/card_balance_heuristic.md and tools/card_heuristic.py as the default curve-check workflow.

note.details: Weak mobility and melee cards were buffed with cleaner identity-aligned changes: Shadow Step became a pure blink, Venom Claw and Tectonic Maul stayed adjacent melee and gained separate setup/payload, and underperforming air manipulation cards picked up real damage or flow so the heuristic bands close without turning melee attacks into pseudo-ranged cards.
note.summary: The April 2026 card rebalance preserves standout freeze, shock, poison, and mobility identities by taxing the hottest cards with health costs instead of stripping effects.

note.details: RunScene owns the instrumentation because it can observe reward picks and before/after combat state. It assigns run/combat ids plus per-combat card instance ids, then logs run/combat/reward events together with card_drawn, card_became_playable, card_played, and enemy_status_tick for offline balancing analysis. spec/analytics.md documents schema version 1; delayed status ticks are currently combat-level rather than card-source attributed.
note.summary: Local card analytics now emit append-only JSONL events through scripts/analytics_store.gd.

note.details: This supports the new 255x255 wall, door, and pillar pixel-art assets without stretching them or rendering doors as low floor markers.
note.summary: Board props now use trimmed PNG art fitted bottom-center in tall tile frames, and visible doors reuse the wall-height prop frame.

note.details: Top/bottom runs use the base wall or door texture, side runs use a horizontal flip for exact style matching, and visible doors still render in the same tall prop frame as walls.
note.summary: Wall and door props now choose row-vs-column orientations from neighboring wall continuity; the perpendicular variant is a mirrored companion of the same processed base art.

note.details: CombatBoardView sorts board tiles by x+y and then x, so the corner fallback in _prop_orientation_variant needs to choose the edge that draws later rather than whichever boundary test runs first. The integrated door art also keeps the same trimmed footprint as wall.png so door tiles inherit the same tall prop frame without spilling past the tile.
note.summary: Boundary wall corners should follow the later-drawn edge orientation, or mirrored wall segments visibly overhang at room corners.

note.details: Wall segments still use the tall prop frame and bottom alignment, but _prop_draw_rect now horizontally compresses boundary blockers after fitting: walls use a slightly reduced width and doors use an even narrower inset width so the opening reads as part of one wall segment instead of spilling across neighbors.
note.summary: Boundary wall and door props render with a narrower draw width than their raw fitted texture so each blocker stays inside a single wall tile span.

note.details: CombatBoardView trims PNG props to their used rect before fitting. The pillar asset loads with a noticeably squarer silhouette than the wall art, but not a perfect 1:1 ratio, so regression coverage should assert that pillars stay materially broader and squarer than wall segments instead of hard-coding a square threshold.
note.summary: Prop-art regression tests should compare trimmed pillar-vs-wall silhouette rather than assuming the pillar stays perfectly square after texture trimming.

note.details: The template library still defines obstacle layouts, but any interior TILE_WALL entry is remapped to TILE_PILLAR during generation so combat rooms only use walls on the outer ring while pillars remain the only interior blocking terrain.
note.summary: Room generation now reserves wall tiles for the perimeter and converts interior template walls into pillars.

note.details: CombatBoardView no longer picks a single wall orientation per boundary tile. Straight perimeter tiles draw one full row or column segment, while corner tiles draw two cropped half-segments from the existing wall art so the outer runs meet cleanly in the middle of the corner tile without the old seam gap.
note.summary: Perimeter walls and doors now render as explicit boundary segments, and corner tiles split into two half-segments that meet at the tile center.

note.details: RoomGenerator returns moss.floor/wall/pillar tile lists, CombatEngine/RunEngine carry that metadata through room and combat state, and CombatBoardView renders seeded moss overlay textures on cinder floors plus wall/pillar props. This replaces the old moss-terrain approach so passability and floor variants stay purely stone.
note.summary: Room moss now lives in decorative metadata instead of terrain tile IDs.

note.details: CombatBoardView keeps the boundary-segment wall/door helpers and tests, but OUTER_WALL_RENDERING_ENABLED is currently false, so _display_tile_id maps outer wall/door tiles to cinder for presentation. This hides the perimeter blockers visually without changing the underlying grid passability or deleting the wall rendering code.
note.summary: Outer boundary wall and door art can stay fully implemented while the default board rendering collapses those edge tiles back to cinder.

note.details: _display_tile_id still resolves hidden boundary doors back to wall semantics, but _tiles_in_draw_order now applies _should_render_tile so only true boundary walls disappear. Active exits and locked presentation doors stay as "door" tiles, which removes the old fake cinder perimeter without breaking traversal.
note.summary: With outer wall rendering disabled, CombatBoardView now hides boundary wall tiles by filtering them out of draw and hit-test order while keeping visible doors rendered and clickable.

note.details: CombatBoardView draws visible "door" tiles from the standalone door.png texture on their own centered frame, leaves the wall boundary-segment path for actual walls only, and reuses the same door sprite for every edge instead of mirroring wall-insert art. This replaced the older wall-height door treatment once the user swapped in a self-contained doorway asset.
note.summary: Visible doors now render as standalone props with a dedicated frame instead of reusing wall-segment rendering.

note.details: The user-supplied door.png had an opaque fake checkerboard background, so the asset was cleaned to real alpha and used as the source/fallback door art. CombatBoardView now loads dedicated door_row.png and door_col.png transformed from that source and renders visible boundary doors through boundary_prop_segments again, so left/right edge doors follow the board perspective instead of reusing the same upright module everywhere.
note.summary: Door presentation now uses a cleaned transparent source plus skewed row/col variants derived from door.png for diagonal boundary exits.

note.details: After the user replaced door.png with a transparent tile-oriented asset, CombatBoardView stopped loading generated door_row.png/door_col.png skew variants. Visible doors now draw as a single overlay prop on the regular cinder floor tile; row-edge doors use door.png as-is for the bottom-left/top-right diagonal, and col-edge doors use AssetLoader.flip_texture_h for the bottom-right/top-left diagonal.
note.summary: Door presentation uses the supplied isometric door.png directly on cinder floor tiles, flipped horizontally for the opposite diagonal.

note.details: CombatBoardView uses DOOR_FRAME_WIDTH_SCALE, DOOR_FRAME_HEIGHT_SCALE, and DOOR_BASELINE_OFFSET_SCALE near the top of the file to fit door.png on top of regular cinder floor tiles. Increasing width/height scales the rendered door; changing baseline moves the planted floor line without touching the source asset or flip logic.
note.summary: Door size and placement are hand-tuned through explicit frame scale constants.

note.details: CombatBoardView no longer calls _draw_exit_marker_for_tile from _draw_scene_objects, so visible door exits keep their icon drawn by _draw_tile_props but no longer render the direction/element label box. The marker function remains in the file if labels need to be restored later.
note.summary: Door exits show only floating element icons, with rectangular exit label boxes disabled.

note.details: The card/UI schema stores pattern as JSON offset pairs and optional rotate. CombatEngine validates ranged AOE centers by range/LOS, applies close AOE from the player tile, and exposes aoe_tiles_for_player_action so RunScene previews and animations use the same best-rotation tile set as damage resolution.
note.summary: AOE card actions use explicit pattern offsets: range 0 resolves from the player without a target, while range > 0 targets a visible center tile; rotate=true patterns auto-select the rotation that hits the most relevant units.

note.details: Card upgrade purchases are stored in progression.card_upgrades as base_card_id -> upgrade_id. Decks, rewards, analytics card ids, and saved runs keep base card ids; callers resolve display and combat behavior through GameData.card_def_with_upgrades/card_def_for_progression so collectible upgrades do not add those cards to the starting deck.
note.summary: Permanent card upgrades keep base card ids and resolve through progression.

note.details: CombatBoardView offsets visible door frames by half a tile step toward the outside/back edge for all four perimeter sides: top-right up/right, bottom-right down/right, bottom-left down/left, and top-left up/left. Keep DOOR_BACK_EDGE_OFFSET_SCALE side-aware when retuning door placement so mirrored door orientations preserve the same apparent back-edge alignment.
note.summary: Door props slide toward each perimeter tile's mirrored back edge.

note.details: CombatBoardView offsets visible door frames toward the outside/back edge, but the top pair are tuned slightly forward with DOOR_TOP_BACK_EDGE_OFFSET_SCALE while the right and bottom perimeter doors keep DOOR_BACK_EDGE_OFFSET_SCALE. Keep top-right/top-left mirrored to each other and bottom-right/bottom-left mirrored to each other when retuning door placement.
note.summary: Door props use mirrored back-edge offsets with a smaller top-edge scale.

note.details: RunScene sends RoomIconLibrary icon ids to CombatBoardView for room-exit door icons, and LabyrinthMapView uses the same helper for minimap room icons. Keep non-combat destination icons and minimap icons in this helper so door selection and the map stay visually consistent; cleared minimap rooms should be shown by muted grey styling rather than overlaying an X.
note.summary: Room door and minimap icons are centralized in RoomIconLibrary.

note.details: Permanent card upgrades now live in progression.card_mods as base_card_id -> Array[mod], with legacy progression.card_upgrades kept only for compatibility. Decks, rewards, analytics ids, and saved runs still keep base card ids; callers resolve behavior through GameData.card_def_for_progression so generated stat/status/pattern/action mods can stack without adding collectible cards to the starting deck. The upgrade UI generates card -> element -> option choices from the current card definition, and costs scale by rarity plus per-card upgrade count.
note.summary: Permanent card upgrades stack as generated card mods.

note.details: The source sheet is 1774x887, so CombatBoardView intentionally derives 443x443 frame cells by integer-dividing 4 columns by 2 rows and ignores the tiny right/bottom padding. Side-edge doors use horizontally flipped frame textures, matching the static door_col orientation.
note.summary: Door opening animation slices door_opening.png as 8 row-major frames from a padded 4x2 sheet.

note.details: door_opening.png is not a reliable equal-cell sheet. CombatBoardView slices the alpha-tight sprite bounds, places each frame on the max 256x383 transparent canvas anchored bottom-right, and scales the shared canvas from frame 0's used height against the static door used rect. Source-oriented doors anchor right/bottom; flipped side doors anchor left/bottom so the door footprint does not resize or drift while opening.
note.summary: Door opening animation normalizes each source frame onto a shared anchored canvas.

note.details: The script emits fonts/LabyrinthCrumble-Regular.ttf, the embedded Godot FontFile .tres, and fonts/LabyrinthCrumble-preview.png from deterministic pixel glyph plans. The imagegen concept sheet is preserved as fonts/LabyrinthCrumble-reference.png for art direction.
note.summary: Labyrinth Crumble is generated from tools/build_labyrinth_font.py; regenerate font artifacts instead of hand-editing the TTF/TRES binaries.

note.details: The generator emits Regular and Header TTF/TRES files plus the preview PNG. Regular remains the default theme font, while UiTypography routes card names, button text, title/room headers, and enemy intent titles through the Header face for a heavier stone display style. Do not hand-edit generated font binaries.
note.summary: Labyrinth Crumble ships generated regular and header font faces; regenerate artifacts with tools/build_labyrinth_font.py.

note.details: The board layout uses the extents of _tiles_in_draw_order() so hidden outer walls no longer make the room look smaller. Tile width can grow to 190px, and _board_origin biases the fitted content upward while preserving top clearance for unit HUDs and bottom clearance above the hand.
note.summary: CombatBoardView board zoom now fits rendered tiles instead of the raw hidden-wall grid.

note.details: Board zoom still uses _tiles_in_draw_order() extents so hidden outer walls do not shrink the room, but those tiles/extents/tile width/origin must stay cached per state and Control.size. Calling _tiles_in_draw_order() or rebuilding extents from _tile_width()/_tile_center() hot draw paths caused severe animation and input lag.
note.summary: CombatBoardView board zoom fits rendered tiles through a cached layout.

note.details: Non-character card, icon, relic, tile loot, and UI chrome assets now live under assets/art as generated PNGs. Remaining SVG references under assets/placeholders/units are intentional because the user explicitly asked not to replace player, enemy, or NPC character art during this overhaul.
note.summary: Generated PNG overhaul intentionally leaves character art references untouched.

note.details: The current card frame uses assets/art/ui/card_frame.png as a texture stylebox while ArtFrame and DetailsPanel stay visually empty, so card art floats in the upper third and ability details share the parchment below. Keep dense icon-summary rows split into short segments; otherwise larger 26px ability icons can overflow narrow card interiors. The rarity indicator is now a visible bottom notch, so do not reserve vertical space by hiding rarity UI.
note.summary: CardWidget art sits on one continuous parchment frame with wrapped icon rows.

note.details: RunScene sets HandBox separation negative only in combat and computes hand card width with that overlap included, so cards can be wider without spreading across the full bottom bar. CardWidget's local hover/selected lift sets z_index=20, which keeps the active card visually in front of its overlapping neighbors.
note.summary: Combat hand cards intentionally overlap, relying on CardWidget hover z-index.

note.details: Character shadows derive from each unit draw rect's planted bottom edge and use skewed isometric ground polygons. note.details: Unit shadows are based on AssetLoader.build_alpha_polygons for the current unit texture or idle AtlasTexture frame, cached per texture instance, then projected from the sprite's planted foot point onto the isometric ground. Generic ground ellipses are only a fallback; pillars, doors, walls, and scene props still use procedural ground-plane shadows drawn before the prop art.
note.summary: CombatBoardView unit shadows use alpha-silhouette projection.

note.details: Silhouette shadow data stores both alpha polygons and their opaque bounds. Normalize polygon points around the opaque bounds, scale by the opaque draw size, and anchor at the opaque-foot point inside the drawn texture rect; do not anchor shadows to draw_rect.end because generated unit sheets include transparent bottom padding. Height cast is slightly leftward to avoid making asymmetric silhouettes read horizontally flipped.
note.summary: CombatBoardView unit shadow anchors use opaque sprite bounds.

note.details: Unit shadow projection is intentionally wider/deeper with minimal sideways shear so shadows read on top of tiles. Shadow foot anchoring uses the median opaque-bottom ratio across a unit type's idle frames, falling back to base/current texture bounds, so transient low-contact pixels such as crawler claw frames can animate the silhouette without moving the whole shadow.
note.summary: CombatBoardView unit shadows are broad silhouettes with stable idle anchors.

note.details: GameData records relic card-action changes under action._modifiers by field, while RunScene passes conditional combat bonuses such as Ember Lens through ActionIconLibrary token options like damage_modifiers. ActionIconLibrary merges both paths into token tone, modified markers, and per-token tooltips so future non-card modifiers should extend token metadata instead of adding card-level modifier tooltip paths.
note.summary: Card UI modifiers are token-level metadata.

note.details: UI should not color elemental intensity costs, gains, or gated-effect numbers green; only separate non-intensity modifiers such as relic buffs should use the boosted-number treatment. Keep intensity payoff rows visually distinct through icon/box styling instead of bonus-number color.
note.summary: Elemental intensity numbers use neutral tone

note.details: Headless target shortcuts should preserve the strategy guide's never-step-on-traps priority by preferring lower trap-risk movement paths before comparing movement distance/path length. This avoids playtest agents accidentally selecting an auto shortcut through a trap when a longer safe shortcut exists.
note.summary: Shortcut plans rank trap-free paths before shortest movement

note.details: Do not render the combat board's top-left idle/hover status labels such as Pick Card, Drag Card, Pass, or hovered/selected card names. They overlap the elemental intensity HUD and the user considers them low-value; keep animation banners and non-combat labels separate.
note.summary: Hide combat board idle status text

note.details: Elemental intensity conditional blocks should keep 3-value-token rows slightly tighter than regular card rows, and render their values as light text with a dark outline for readability against the mostly opaque elemental background.
note.summary: Conditional card rows prefer compact light text

note.details: Elemental intensity conditional rows should choose summary icon/label metrics against both available height and available visual width, including scaled card widgets such as discard pile previews. Requirement tokens can carry condition_active from RunScene; CardWidget uses it only for active glow styling, while inactive rows keep the same compact block layout.
note.summary: Conditional card rows size against visual width and active state

note.details: When a non-boss ring room has no revealed, unsealed same-depth-or-deeper exits after entry, combat victory, or loaded-run repair, RunEngine persists a loop_escape outward connection, reveals that destination, and stamps the door into current_room_layout. Static room_metadata still reports only the normal one-quarter outward links until run state needs the escape.
note.summary: Loop-closing rooms can gain dynamic outward escape links

note.details: RunScene detects fatigue for presentation by comparing before/after deck.cycles around CombatEngine.prepare_next_player_turn, then plays player impact, floating text, and the full-screen edge overlay. CombatEngine remains the source of fatigue damage rules; avoid adding visual-only state to combat dictionaries unless gameplay or analytics need it.
note.summary: Fatigue damage visuals key off deck cycle deltas.

note.details: RunScene now presents campfire choices through the shared RelicChoiceOverlay instead of ContextChoiceOverlay buttons. Linger for a moment calls RunEngine.leave_campfire with a 10 HP heal and continues; Embrace the fire's warmth keeps the old fire-rest banking/unlock flow, showing ??? until rested_at_fire/card_upgrades_unlocked is true.
note.summary: Campfire choices use relic-style panels.

note.details: RunScene stages moving actors at their destination before rendering movement frames, then uses CombatBoardView presentation unit_world_positions to interpolate the visible sprite and unit_draw_tiles for final layering. CombatBoardView exposes footprint-aware world_position_for_unit_origin and draw_tile_for_unit_origin so large enemies such as Zekarion animate from their visual footprint center and draw on the destination front tile instead of snapping to the anchor/origin if a presentation frame is missed.
note.summary: Movement animation state is staged at destination.

note.details: CombatEngine increments elemental_intensity_gained_total whenever intensity is raised and elemental_intensity_spent_total whenever relic threshold rewards consume intensity. RunScene card_played analytics compares those counters so raise-and-consume relic payoffs do not disappear into a net before/after elemental_intensity delta.
note.summary: Intensity-spending relics track gross gain and spend counters.

note.details: Root-level HUD overlays such as elemental intensity and combat choice buttons should not rely on a single immediate get_global_rect() from container placeholders after refresh. Relic/header reflow and ChoiceBar placeholder layout can settle a frame later, so connect resized signals and provide nearby fallback anchors like relic child bottoms or PilesBar to avoid stale gaps or top-screen jumps.
note.summary: RunScene root overlays need resize-driven relayouts.

note.details: Use transparent pixel-art decals rendered over the board's existing tiles; the user specifically rejected simple vector/line effects and generated tile/floor backgrounds for these blasts.
note.summary: Battlefield trap blast VFX should use raster sprite assets without baked tile backgrounds or simple vector primitive overlays.

note.details: CombatBoardView builds obstruction entries from visible units, scene props, destructible terrain, loot, and traps. Tall foreground props (walls, pillars, doors, scene props, terrain) use those entries to fade when overlapping earlier-drawn board contents, not just characters.
note.summary: Foreground obstruction fading is entry-based across board contents.

note.details: Tall foreground props fade only when their overlap covers at least 25% of the behind entry rect, such as a unit, prop, loot item, trap, or terrain sprite. The threshold is intentionally based on the covered object's sprite rect rather than tile area so tiny edge slivers remain opaque.
note.summary: Foreground obstruction fading uses covered-sprite coverage threshold.

note.details: CombatBoardView hides full-health idle terrain bars, shows them for damaged terrain or attack-highlighted terrain, and reads projected loss from damage_preview entries keyed as terrain_<id>. RunScene includes those terrain_<id> entries in player attack previews so terrain bars can render the same pending-loss overlay as unit health bars.
note.summary: Terrain health bars are contextual and preview-driven.

note.details: The manual harness board legend and combat state output intentionally list pickups, destructible terrain, and attackable adjacent-blast traps so text playtests preserve the same tactical information exposed in the board UI. Card resolution and analytics payloads also include terrain damage, terrain destruction, triggered traps, and collected pickups.
note.summary: Headless playtest mirrors battlefield readability changes

note.details: The client board hover tooltip should show compact facts such as object name, HP, damage, and status effects. Extra guidance like terrain movement/LoS rules or trap trigger instructions belongs in tools/headless_playtest.gd and playtest docs instead of the normal game tooltip.
note.summary: Keep normal game hover tooltips concise; put tactical instructions in playtest surfaces.

note.details: Campfire choice panels remain relic-style, but the third Draw strength from the flame option opens the level-up overlay when held embers meet ProgressionStore.next_level_cost. Linger heals 100 and continues; Embrace carries the current held ember count into the next run; Draw Strength spends held embers, assigns one stat point, exits campfire mode without healing, and continues the run.
note.summary: Campfires now choose between heal, carry, or level up.

note.details: Cards and enemy definitions are scaled from old small data values through GameData before combat/UI use: HP, damage, block, heal, health cost, burn, poison, terrain and pickup amounts are 10x, while embers, draw/card-play counts, movement/range, freeze, shock, chain, and intensity remain unscaled. Progression stat bonuses are intentionally small displayed increments applied after this base scaling.
note.summary: Fixed-point scaling lives at data load boundaries.

note.details: data/relics.json descriptions may contain placeholders like {value}, {0.value}, {action.amount}, and {0.reward0.amount}. Player-facing relic copy should come from GameData.relic_def(), which replaces placeholders with effect-derived display values and applies fixed-point scaling for health, damage, block, stoneskin, burn, poison, and relevant reward/action amounts; GameData.relics() remains raw data.
note.summary: Relic descriptions are formatted display templates.

note.details: Progression level purchases use GameData.progression_stat_points_per_level from data/progression_levels.json, currently 2. Campfire Draw Strength requires choosing two different non-capped stats before confirm; ProgressionStore.purchase_level_with_stats validates the distinct stat list and allocates both points in the same purchase.
note.summary: Character levels now assign two distinct stat points.

note.details: RunEngine stages ProgressionStore recovery_marker data into the next run as room metadata at the death coordinate, forcing that room to a combat encounter and injecting dropped_embers loot into its combat layout. Combat collection increments combat_state.recovered_embers_total; RunEngine.set_combat_state applies only the new delta to held embers and clears the progression marker after reclaim.
note.summary: Lost embers are recovered through staged run recovery markers.

note.details: RoomGenerator no longer center-biases pickup/trap/terrain scoring or excludes playable corner floor tiles for destructible terrain. Terrain still avoids occupied tiles, the current entry halo, and placements that disconnect the remaining open floor.
note.summary: Tile pickups, traps, and destructible terrain can occupy playable edge-band floor tiles.

note.details: move_toward evaluates all actually reachable anchors, avoids traps, scores by remaining route to the target, and uses destructible terrain only as a planning hint so enemies can move up to blockers before attack actions break them. enemy_threat_tiles intentionally previews full movement reach and all attack tiles from the movement frontier instead of filtering by whether each move gets closer to the current player tile.
note.summary: Enemy advance movement is route-scored, while threat previews show full reach.

note.details: enemy_threat_tiles routes movement endpoints into attack previews for melee, ranged, aoe, push, pull, and lightning_strikes. Attack previews build a temporary enemy at each anchor so large footprints such as Zekarion threaten from every occupied square; lightning_strikes previews use the deterministic _lightning_strike_tiles result instead of hiding or overgeneralizing the special attack.
note.summary: Enemy threat previews mirror full movement, footprints, and special attacks.

note.details: Tempest Breath uses move_toward 1 plus ranged range 3 because Zekarion's 2x2 gameplay footprint otherwise turns range 4+ into near room-wide coverage on open boss boards. Tests assert the opposite corner can remain outside the preview and actual hit.
note.summary: Zekarion Tempest Breath is intentionally short-range.

note.details: enemy_threat_tiles uses a threat-only blocker set that erases the current player position while preserving terrain, traps, enemies, and illusions. This keeps red threat zones conservative for move/blink destinations: if the player merely relocates without opening or closing paths, enemy movement previews include routes through the old player tile so destinations they can hit are marked.
note.summary: Enemy threat previews assume the player may vacate their current tile.

note.details: enemy_threat_tiles uses a threat-only blocker set that erases the current player position while preserving terrain, traps, enemies, and illusions, so move/blink destinations account for routes through the old player tile. Attack previews also include blast tiles for traps an enemy can safely trigger from any reachable endpoint, keeping red zones conservative for enemy actions that can damage the moved player without the player changing blockers.
note.summary: Enemy threat previews assume player relocation and enemy-triggered hazards.

note.details: Air room enemies keep their +1 movement at medium/deep encounter depths, but elementalized attacks are fixed to range 3 so their max normal-roster move+attack reach is 8 instead of 9. Lightning room enemies keep high attack ranges, but positive move_toward/move_away actions lose 1 tile with a floor of 1 so their max normal-roster reach is 6.
note.summary: Elemental enemy reach budgets preserve movement safety.

note.details: Air room enemies keep their +1 movement at medium/deep encounter depths, but elementalized attacks stay in a 3-4 range band so their max normal-roster move+attack reach is 8 instead of 9. Lightning room enemies keep high attack ranges, but positive move_toward/move_away actions lose 1 tile with a floor of 1 so their max normal-roster reach is 6.
note.summary: Elemental enemy reach budgets preserve movement safety.

Runtime orientation is stored only on resolved action copies: orientation for rotatable AOE, force_direction for push/pull. Analytics play-mode comparisons erase those fields so printed cards stay classified as printed.

note.details: Manual headless console mirrors real drag lanes: drag play uses printed text, drag attack uses the fixed-point fallback attack for 20 damage from base 2, and drag move remains range 2. Keep play-mode analytics comparisons aligned with those generated fallback action helpers instead of hardcoded raw arrays.
note.summary: Headless drag fallback attack uses fixed-point damage.

AOE orientation is chosen while aiming: hover centers the pattern, left/right or mouse-drag rotates it, and click stores orientation on the resolved action. Push/pull use force_direction, with only legal away/toward directions offered.

note.details: Cards express immobilize as immobilize: true, not a numeric stack. Combat stores it as a one-turn boolean unit condition consumed at the affected unit's next activation; enemies skip movement actions only, while player restriction blocks move and blink actions.
note.summary: Immobilize is a boolean one-turn movement lock

note.details: For ranged card art, do not default to a hooded attacker on the left firing across a detailed scene at an enemy on the right. Vary compositions toward close-ups, over-the-shoulder views, environmental silhouettes, impact moments, or other card-specific framing unless that side-profile duel is explicitly requested.
note.summary: Avoid repeated side-profile ranged duel card art compositions

note.details: Hamstring Shot replaces Bone Dart in GameData.starting_deck as the starter ranged card. Bone Dart remains defined with rarity starter so old saves, tests, or debug fixtures can still load it, but it is not marked starter and should not appear in starting_deck or reward_card_pool_by_rarity unless intentionally revived.
note.summary: Bone Dart is retired from active starter/reward pools

note.details: For the initiative UI, portraits are sprite-derived thumbnails from assets/placeholders/units via tools/build_turn_order_assets.gd. Avoid generated reinterpretations that change character silhouette, tone, or style.
note.summary: Turn order portraits should match the in-game unit sprites.

note.details: Initiative turn-order changes should emit explicit turn_order steps from CombatEngine with before_order/after_order arrays. RunScene consumes those snapshots for pop/reslot animation instead of inferring from its possibly stale _combat_state during enemy animations, which prevents the player portrait from remaining active at the head after finish_player_activation.
note.summary: Turn-order UI animates from engine-provided order snapshots.

note.details: Printed player cards now use a wider initiative-time curve: fast cards are around 1-3, normal cards around 5, and heavy commitments around 8-10. Runtime scheduling remains current_clock + player_base_initiative + total card time, so two average cards make card time roughly as important as the base delay while Agility still matters. The card heuristic baseline is 5 with a 0.45 tempo delta.
note.summary: Card time now uses a 1-10 scale with baseline 5.

note.details: With initiative turns, revealed enemy intents are previews only. Block is cleared at the start of that enemy activation, applied by resolving the enemy block action, and persists until that same enemy's next activation starts. _apply_revealed_intent_blocks remains a no-op compatibility shim.
note.summary: Enemy guard intents must not materialize block before activation

note.details: current_turn_order now includes the active/current slot plus projected follow-up slots for live actors. Queued enemies get a second projected activation at queued_time + base_initiative + current intent time, and the active player gets a projected next slot using base initiative plus time already spent plus any RunScene card-hover preview delta.
note.summary: Turn-order previews show up to two activations per actor

note.details: The turn-order widget intentionally removes entries by sliding/fading them upward while their slot remains, rebuilds the final order, inverts surviving portraits from their old global positions so only the relevant entries slide into place, then fades/drops inserted entries into the opened slot. Avoid reverting to custom_minimum_size collapse/expand because that reads like a static reorder instead of a game-style queue update.
note.summary: Turn-order animation uses staged FLIP reflow

note.details: Turn-order transitions must not infer removals from exact projected queue snapshots because projected times/seqs can change for multiple future entries. RunScene now uses active-head removal for the pop/fade, treats activation-only head changes as a style update, matches survivors by actor plus scheduled/projected role, and locks the panel width during reflow so the widget does not shrink or grow mid-animation.
note.summary: Turn-order animation removes only the active head entry

note.details: Player base initiative is 9 with Agility reducing it to a floor of 5. Starter card times now average about 4.1; Whirlwind Slash is normal-speed at 5 and Bloody Lunge is the heavy starter at 8. First-sequence weighted repeat cycles are about wisp 11, crawler 13, harrier 13.4, acolyte 16.25, warden 20.25, and Zekarion 19.25, so normal two-card starter turns should usually return before the same fast enemy follows up while heavy+normal turns can let fast enemies double-up.
note.summary: Initiative balance now favors standard early player returns

note.details: Four-enemy rooms show 10 turn entries including the player and fit acceptably; five-enemy rooms showing 12 were too wide, so cap the visible turn-order widget at 10 rather than 8.
note.summary: Turn order header cap is 10 visible slots

note.details: Turn order portrait numbers should display each entry's eta from the current initiative clock, not absolute scheduled time from combat start. Tooltips can still include the absolute Clock line as secondary context.
note.summary: Turn Clock portrait badges show relative ETA

note.details: The card time-cost badge is intentionally drawn as a larger procedural clock face that can overhang the card's top-right frame. CardWidget root clipping is disabled while art/title/detail controls keep their own clipping, and the clock hands animate while the card is hovered.
note.summary: Card time costs use an overhanging animated clock badge

note.details: The card time-cost badge hover animation advances one accelerated clock seconds value at 24 simulated seconds per real second. The second, minute, and hour hands are derived from that same value, so minute/hour movement stays proportional and the hands do not each run independent loops.
note.summary: Clock badge animation uses real hand ratios

note.details: To keep the time-cost badge asset-free while matching raster card art better, draw it as layered brass/recess circles with directional highlight/shadow arcs, tick shadows, tapered polygon hands, a second-hand shadow, and a small dark number medallion. This avoids imagegen while making the badge feel less flat.
note.summary: Procedural time clock uses layered bevel shading

note.details: The card time-cost clock should keep only a small overhang past the frame, with matching top and right overhang. Avoid pushing it much farther right than upward; the balanced placement sits better on the card frame.
note.summary: Time badge overhang should be symmetrical

note.details: The create-labyrinth-card skill now treats top-level card time as required card data, explains the 1-10 initiative-cost scale with 5 baseline, asks final reports to justify the chosen time, and notes that CardWidget renders the clock badge at runtime rather than through card art.
note.summary: Card creation skill requires time costs

note.details: Enemy target selection gathers all closest valid player-side actor targets, including the player and live illusions, and uses combat RNG to choose among equal-distance ties. This applies movement, attack, push, and pull target selection, so illusions must be strictly closer only when reliable redirection is required.
note.summary: Enemy target ties among player-side actors are randomized

note.details: Early playtest runs repeatedly died to depth-two fire burn spirals before reaching the first boss. Fire enemy attacks now use a one-player-scale burn payload at encounter depths 1-2 and only restore the heavier burn payload at deeper standard rooms, while keeping the direct fire damage bump at depth 2.
note.summary: Depth-two fire rooms keep shallow burn pressure

note.details: Fire traps now apply one-player-scale burn at depths 1-2 and reserve the heavier burn payload for deeper fire rooms, matching the combat-engine fire enemy burn ramp used after early playtest deaths from depth-two burn attrition.
note.summary: Depth-two fire traps keep shallow burn pressure

note.details: Enemy target selection gathers all closest valid player-side actor targets, including the player and live illusions, and uses combat RNG to choose among equal-distance ties. This applies movement, attack, push, and pull target selection, so illusions must be strictly closer only when reliable redirection is required.
note.summary: Enemy target ties among player-side actors are randomized

note.details: Fire traps now apply one-player-scale burn at depths 1-2 and reserve the heavier burn payload for deeper fire rooms, matching the combat-engine fire enemy burn ramp used after early playtest deaths from depth-two burn attrition.
note.summary: Depth-two fire traps keep shallow burn pressure

note.details: The manual playtest harness exposes campfire linger healing and level-up commands in addition to leave/rest. First-boss playtests should use campfires as continue-value rooms rather than forced run endpoints, reserving rest for banking and ending the run.
note.summary: Headless campfire choices mirror live continue options

note.details: The manual playtest harness now mirrors the live turn-order widget more closely: combat state prints the current order plus pass-return timing, and each playable card row prints where the player's next turn lands after that card's time cost. Action text also surfaces pierce, immobilize, push, and pull keywords, with pierce defense-bypass included in target hints, card resolution notes, and analytics payloads.
note.summary: Headless console previews turn-order timing and combat keywords

note.details: RunEngine's dynamic loop_escape now treats deeper exits, cleared rooms, free-value rooms such as treasure/campfire, and NPC rooms as preferred progress. If the only same-depth options are uncleared combat/boss rooms, the current room persists a revealed outward loop_escape so players can choose progression instead of being forced through lateral combat chains.
note.summary: Combat-only lateral routes gain an outward choice

note.details: Combat hand output includes hand cap, draw/discard/burned counts, and next fatigue damage. Range-0 AOE action text lists affected tiles from the current state, and target-needing follow-up actions with no legal targets now pause with an explicit skip/cancel prompt instead of silently committing only earlier card effects.
note.summary: Headless console exposes deck pressure and partial action skips

note.details: Target labels in the manual harness now treat every tile in an enemy footprint as that enemy, so 2x2 bosses such as Zekarion are not shown as anonymous coordinates when targetable through a non-origin footprint tile.
note.summary: Headless target labels include large enemy footprints

note.details: 2026-05-29 restarted playtest loop reverted the dynamic combat-only outward route shortcut. Balance changes made depth 1 easier, reward/build cards stronger, fatigue lower, crawler lunge blockable, and depth-3 generic scaling moderated. In honest r2, seed 5293102 cleared first boss after 7 pre-boss combats and 12 rooms including start; winning deck used Thunderline, Volt Surge, Static Lash, Hearth Rush, Hamstring Slice, Mirror Shard, and Updraft Bottle. Other r2 agents still mostly died to first depth-3 fire, so depth-3 fire remains the main wall despite goal success.
note.summary: Honest first-boss clear achieved after reverting pathing shortcut and retuning early combat.

note.details: The design-only pack under output/buildaround_cards_100 keeps cards out of data/cards.json but uses proposed_cards_game_ready.json entries with a novel text_rule action plus presentation.mode=text_rule. Current CardWidget can only be coerced for previews with renderer-only overrides; selected build-around cards will need a real text-summary/card presentation mode so costs and rules text coexist before merging into the live pool.
note.summary: Text build-around card pack uses staged text_rule actions

note.details: Draw-card/card-proxy animations can continue after RunScene loads a non-combat state in probes or fast transitions. Guard FX loops with the current mode and layer liveness, and hide/drop top_level on proxy subtrees before queue_free so stale cards do not reappear over reward, campfire, or terminal overlays.
note.summary: Card FX coroutines must stop on mode changes

note.details: The combat hand uses rotated rightmost cards with left-to-right z-order, so the visual edge can extend past the fan container's nominal card bounds even when card sizes fit. Keep an asymmetric right-overflow allowance in HandFanContainer's minimum/content width so CenterContainer shifts the fan slightly left and prevents edge cards from clipping at the viewport.
note.summary: Hand fan measured width includes asymmetric right overflow

note.details: Calling RunScene._animate_enemy_phase_steps from a visual probe can overlap turn-order rebuild coroutines and produce freed Control casts that do not reflect normal gameplay. For motion screenshots, prefer deterministic direct helpers such as _animate_move_step with a duplicated combat state, then restore the board before sampling later effects.
note.summary: Motion probes should sample isolated animation helpers

note.details: Enemy name/intent/HP labels occupy the tile center above units, especially near the lower board edge. Place enemy HP/block/stoneskin floaters in an above-HUD lane and keep renderer outlines enabled so impact feedback stays readable over floors and unit sprites.
note.summary: Enemy damage floaters must clear the HUD stack.

note.details: Top-level card FX controls can survive a draw/play animation and later appear as ghost hand cards during selection; keep cleanup gated by _animation_lock so active tweens are preserved but idle refreshes scrub leftovers.
note.summary: Idle hand refreshes must clear stale CardFxLayer proxies once animations unlock.

note.details: tests/ui_probe.gd now recursively clears user://probes and owns fresh door_opening frame captures. Old nested folders such as door_opening or targeting can otherwise be copied into new visual-polish pass folders and make stale screenshots look authoritative.
note.summary: UI probe output must clear nested artifact folders.

note.details: Player-facing card action values use the universal 10x combat scale: Quick Stab should display 90 damage, not 9. Treat the trailing zero on fixed-point-scaled damage/heal/block/status values as intentional unless the design changes explicitly.
note.summary: Card combat numbers intentionally display fixed-point scale.

note.details: A nearly opaque ColorRect scrim still allowed the high-contrast room header to ghost through above the large-map dialog margin in screenshots. Keep LargeMapScrim alpha at 1.0 unless the modal design changes to intentionally reveal the room behind it.
note.summary: Large map modal backdrop should be fully opaque.

note.details: A 36px bottom overflow allowance let hovered/selected combat cards sit low enough for the viewport edge to clip their lower frame. Keep the default bottom overflow allowance around 6px and tests should guard that outer-card sink remains only slight while preserving the fan shape.
note.summary: Hand fan bottom sink stays tiny to keep card frames readable.

note.details: The campfire Draw Strength overlay includes a confirm/cancel action row and opened low enough in 1920x1080 captures that the 660px character-sheet height clipped the action row. Keep the level_up progression dialog around 560px tall and let the stat list scroll so the action row remains visible.
note.summary: Level-up progression overlay uses a shorter dialog than the character sheet.

note.details: The broad ui_probe sequence captures turn-order/pass-turn frames before Thunderline orientation frames. Without resetting RunScene card resolution plus combat_state current_actor/cards_played_this_turn/death_bonus_card_plays_this_turn/card_play_bonus_this_turn/player_turn_restrictions, _on_card_pressed can no-op and save stale non-selected screenshots even though the renderer works. Reset those fields before selected-card visual probes.
note.summary: Card-selection visual probes must reset player-turn state after pass-turn captures.

note.details: A Thunderline motion sample with low-HP targets killed an enemy, started death/ember reward coroutines, and later motion samples hit a freed mote. For isolated attack-effect frames, use high-HP targets or wait for the full reward sequence; keep lethal fixtures only for explicit death/reward visual QA.
note.summary: AOE motion probes should avoid lethal fixtures unless sampling death rewards.

note.details: Run state stores equipped_equipment, equipment_inventory, collected_equipment, and reward_cards. deck_cards is derived from equipped gear cards plus reward_cards and should be rebuilt through RunEngine after claims or equipment swaps. Equipment cards should set reward_pool:false so normal combat rewards remain elemental-only; equipment swaps are only allowed from room/campfire state.
note.summary: Equipment compiles deck_cards from gear plus reward_cards

note.details: Equipped gear is passed from RunScene into CombatBoardView presentation.equipped_equipment and drawn as slot-anchored, rarity-ringed icon overlays on the player unit. This keeps gear visuals data-driven without regenerating or re-rigging the player idle sprite sheets; future sprite work should preserve the presentation payload or intentionally replace this overlay path.
note.summary: Player equipment visuals render as board presentation overlays

note.details: OS window captures on macOS can cap the viewport height and silently clip lower equipment rows. The gallery proof script renders each slot into an offscreen SubViewport sized from the equipment count before saving, so all rows appear regardless of display height or high-DPI scaling.
note.summary: Equipment gallery proofs should render through a sized SubViewport.

note.details: Equipment should not share granted card IDs across items. Each equipment card should read as something that specific item would enable mechanically and visually: swords grant sword attacks, shields grant blocks/bashes/guards, armor grants bracing/protection/repair, boots grant movement/footwork/trips, and trinkets grant small artifact effects. Avoid mechanically odd pairings such as adjacent melee attacks that pull targets, and keep equipment icons readable as tangible gear in the relic-like object style.
note.summary: Equipment cards should be unique and equipment-themed

note.details: CardWidget now scales margins, title bands, art/details bands, fonts, time badges, and summary icons from one uniform card scale based on the native 250x352 card. RunScene card surfaces should hand CardWidget rectangles normalized to the 352/250 aspect so draw/discard piles, hand cards, tooltips, equipment previews, and upgrade previews do not stretch frames, gems, art, or action rows independently.
note.summary: CardWidget preview sizes must preserve the native card aspect

note.details: For non-default card surfaces, RunScene wraps a native 250x352 CardWidget in a scaled parent instead of directly resizing the CardWidget. This keeps the frame border, rarity gem, art window, title, time badge, and action rows in the same proportions for hand cards, draw/discard piles, pile dialogs, equipment/card tooltips, upgrade previews, and drag/animation proxies. Direct CardWidget resizing can still distort nine-slice frame details.
note.summary: Resized card surfaces should scale native CardWidgets as one object

note.details: Raw 96x96 transparent equipment icons shrink to a dark 58px object on cinder floor tiles and are easy to miss. CombatBoardView should keep equipment pickups larger than consumables and draw a rarity/accent-backed pickup marker behind the actual icon so drops are visibly distinct without replacing the gear art.
note.summary: Equipment tile loot needs a distinct pickup marker

note.details: Equipment room drops remain seed/coordinate deterministic for normal rolls, but RunEngine tracks equipment_drop_misses and forces a weighted equipment drop after two eligible combat rooms without one. Loaded saves missing this counter migrate to the pity threshold so older in-progress runs are not stranded with no equipment after the feature lands.
note.summary: Equipment drops use pity protection

reason: User rejected the crude marker/shape treatment for equipment tile loot; equipment should render as the actual icon with normal pickup placement and shadow.

note.details: User rejected the hand-drawn marker/plate/circle treatment for equipment pickups. Equipment loot should render as the actual equipment icon with the normal loot ground shadow and the same bottom-anchored tile footprint as potion and shield pickups; visibility should be solved by reliable drop placement/rates, not extra board shapes.
note.summary: Equipment tile loot uses icon-only pickup rendering

note.details: Character-sheet equipment drag/drop animations should render temporary icon proxies on EquipmentFxLayer above the character overlay. Do not use CardFxLayer for these room-mode UI animations because RunScene clears CardFxLayer outside combat/reward, which can erase snap/swap proxies during overlay rebuilds.
note.summary: Equipment re-equip animations use a dedicated gear FX layer

note.details: Character-sheet equipment drag should be handled by RunScene with EquipmentHeldProxy/EquipmentSwapProxy controls on EquipmentFxLayer. Avoid Godot native Control drag/drop for gear: its OS cursor feedback can show a forbidden-circle cursor and obscure the intended held-item presentation. The dedicated gear FX layer also avoids CardFxLayer cleanup outside combat/reward.
note.summary: Equipment re-equip drag uses in-scene proxies instead of native Control DnD

note.details: Character-sheet inventory gear should treat the whole equipment tile as one hover/drag surface: child icon, labels, and layout controls are mouse_filter IGNORE, while the EquipmentInventoryTile parent owns tooltip and press/move/release drag. Gear drag uses EquipmentHeldProxy/EquipmentSwapProxy on EquipmentFxLayer instead of Godot native Control DnD so the held icon remains visible and avoids the forbidden OS cursor.
note.summary: Equipment inventory tiles are single pointer targets

note.details: Run state keeps reward_cards as collected reward-card history, while attuned_magic_cards is the six-slot active magic loadout that compiles into deck_cards alongside equipment. magic_inventory holds inactive reserve/default magic cards. Card rewards are claimed into reserve and require an out-of-combat character-sheet swap to become active.
note.summary: Magic rewards now use capped attunement

note.details: The character sheet keeps Gear focused on equipment and a read-only current deck. Magic management lives in its own tab with six attuned spell slots, a learned/reserve spell panel, and the same read-only deck column; reserve/default magic tiles should not be created as drag targets on Gear.
note.summary: Magic swaps live in a dedicated Magic tab

note.details: Magic loadout swaps must let any MagicCardTile complete an active drag on left-button release, not only the tile that began the drag. Godot can deliver the release to the hovered destination spell tile, so target tiles need to call _release_magic_overlay_drag when _magic_overlay_drag_active is true.
note.summary: Magic drag release can land on the destination tile

note.details: For character-sheet Magic swaps, resolving only the cursor point is too strict because players position the translucent held spell over a slot/panel. The drop resolver should prefer exact tile hits, then held-card overlap, then the nearest opposite-side tile when the held card or cursor is inside the attuned/learned panel.
note.summary: Magic drops should resolve by visible held-card overlap

note.details: The Magic tab can receive the same mouse-up through both RunScene._input and MagicCardTile._gui_input while _release_magic_overlay_drag awaits the snap animation. Without a release-in-progress guard or marking input handled before awaits, the first release swaps the spells and the second release can swap them right back, appearing as a brief successful text change followed by a snapback.
note.summary: Async magic drag releases must be single-shot

note.details: Gear/Magic deck badges, Magic loadout tiles, and the held magic proxy now reuse each card's art_path as a cropped horizontal background with a dark wash and accent strip, rather than maintaining separate badge assets. New card art should keep a recognizable cue in the central y≈48..96 source band so the character-menu crop reads well.
note.summary: Character menu card badges reuse card art

note.details: Gear/Magic deck badges, Magic loadout tiles, and the held magic proxy crop each card's art_path behind the name. The inner wash should use a faint full-surface accent tint plus dark readability wash; avoid hard left/bottom accent strips because they read as crude overlapping lines. The colored border carries the explicit accent.
note.summary: Character menu card badges use soft accent tint, not hard strips

note.details: Gear/Magic deck badges, Magic loadout tiles, and held magic proxies now put ElementData.card_art_background plus a dim overscanned copy of the card art behind the sharp art crop, then apply the dark readability wash and label. This avoids black side gutters from ragged transparent card art while preserving the no-hard-strips visual direction.
note.summary: Character menu card badges fill transparent art edges with muted backing

note.details: Gear/Magic deck badges and magic tiles should avoid hard horizontal shadow cuts or obvious backing/underpaint seams. The backing uses per-strip gradients, the wash uses soft vertical and side shadow ramps, and the dim overscanned art fill stays low-opacity so it supports transparent art edges without reading as a separate layer.
note.summary: Character menu badge fills should blend without visible bands

note.details: Labyrinth parallel task infrastructure lives in .codex/skills/parallel-labyrinth-task plus tools/parallel_task.py, tools/godot_task_runner.py, and tools/visual_probe_runner.py. Godot commands should run through the wrappers so each process gets a task-local HOME under /private/tmp/labyrinth-godot-home, a safe --log-file, and LABYRINTH_TASK_ID; setting LABYRINTH_TASK_ID without a temp HOME/log file can crash or fail under the sandbox when Godot rotates user:// logs before the runtime hook can create directories.
note.summary: Parallel Codex task workflow uses isolated worktrees and temp-HOME Godot runs

note.details: New git worktrees do not have .godot/global_script_class_cache.cfg, so headless --script runs can report missing class_name types while exiting 0. Built-in tests/probes that must run in fresh worktrees should preload typed classes directly, and Godot wrappers should scan output for SCRIPT ERROR, Parse Error, Failed to load script, or TEST RESULT: FAIL instead of trusting exit code alone.
note.summary: Fresh Godot worktrees lack generated global-class cache

note.details: tools/godot_task_runner.py and tools/visual_probe_runner.py generate default run/user-dir namespaces with nanosecond time plus process id, with the unique fragment early in the name so Godot custom_user_dir truncation cannot erase it. Same-task visual probes may run concurrently through the wrapper; avoid hand-picked identical --run-id values unless intentionally sharing state.
note.summary: Parallel Godot wrappers use process-unique run namespaces

note.details: For Labyrinth queue orchestration, implementation workers must run as user-visible Codex app threads with callable create_thread, read_thread, and send_message_to_thread equivalents exposed by the host session. If those tools are missing, stop before leasing/launching and report a blocker; do not silently fall back to hidden sub-agents, pre-created worktrees, terminal-only workers, or manual user-created threads without explicit same-turn user approval.
note.summary: Autonomous implementation workers must be app-visible threads

note.details: For Labyrinth queue orchestration, a request to use -labyrinth-tasks, run queued work, launch workers, start background tasks, or parallelize the queue is enough permission to create user-visible Codex app/background threads. Do not make the user separately say 'create background threads' each time; still stop if the host session does not expose create/read/send app-thread tools.
note.summary: Orchestration requests authorize visible background threads

note.details: For Labyrinth queue orchestration, a request to use $orchestrate-labyrinth-tasks, run queued work, launch workers, start background tasks, or parallelize the queue is enough permission to create user-visible Codex app/background threads. Do not make the user separately say "create background threads" each time; still stop if the host session does not expose create/read/send app-thread tools.
