note.summary: Orchestration requests authorize visible background threads

note.details: User explicitly said to forget the collision concept for autonomous Labyrinth task orchestration and rely on normal git merge resolution. Keep queue schema fields valid if required, but do not block launching reviewed work because tasks may touch the same large files such as scripts/run_scene.gd.
note.summary: Do not gate Labyrinth task orchestration on collisions

note.details: Enemy and player action animations can render an animated display_state that intentionally differs from _combat_state, with unit_world_positions/unit_draw_tiles carrying the in-flight sprite position. Hover signals from the board, hand, or rebuilt turn-order slots may still fire while _animation_lock is true; those callbacks may update hover bookkeeping but must not call _refresh_stage_view until the lock is released, or they can redraw stale _combat_state over the active animation and cause a visible rewind/snap.
note.summary: Animation-locked hover callbacks must not refresh the board

note.details: Player card resolution can leave _preview_combat_state at the fully resolved position while _play_player_card sets _animation_lock and refreshes UI before _animate_player_card_resolution. During animation lock, _board_display_state should prefer authoritative _combat_state and let explicit _render_board_state calls provide in-flight frames; otherwise the player can flash at the destination, rewind, then animate there.
note.summary: Animation-locked board display must ignore resolved card previews

note.details: Initial enemy queue slots now use enemy base initiative plus revealed intent time, with only an enemy-index stagger for readability; repeats already used the same base+intent cycle. Player base initiative remains 9 with Agility floor 5. The June 2026 speed rebalance broadened card times so the starting deck averages about 3.56 time, the full card pool has 32 cards at time 1-3, and reward-eligible cards include time-2 Threaded Path, time-3 Stone Plate, and eleven time-4 options. Practical pacing target: two fast cards return around initiative 13 and can lap slower enemies, two medium cards return around 18 without fast enemy double-ups, and two slow cards around 23 can let wisps/crawlers threaten doubles.
note.summary: Initiative balance now uses intent-aware first enemy timing and a wider fast-card pool

note.details: Initial enemy queue slots use enemy base initiative plus revealed intent time, with only an enemy-index stagger for readability; repeats use the same base+intent cycle. Player base initiative remains 9 with Agility floor 5. The June 2026 speed rebalance broadened card times so the starting deck averages about 3.56 time and normal elemental combat rewards span the full 1-10 range: Threaded Path is a time-1 Air movement/draw reward, Thorn Skewer is time 2, Firebrand Volley/Rime Shard/Spark Focus/Stone Plate are time 3, White Silence is time 9, and Wildfire Halo remains time 10. Practical pacing target: two fast cards return around initiative 13 and can lap slower enemies, two medium cards return around 18 without fast enemy double-ups, and two slow cards around 23 can let wisps/crawlers threaten doubles.
note.summary: Initiative balance now uses intent-aware first enemy timing and live fast elemental rewards

note.details: For campfire room polish, do not render the bonfire glow as visible tile rings, hard circles, or an orange wash. Use blended soft light and visible ember motes that reuse the fire elemental room particle language so the effect reads organic and professional.
note.summary: Campfire firelight should avoid banded halos

note.details: For campfire ember motes, avoid an inverted-triangle plume where every spark starts at one center point and spreads outward. Prefer a slightly wider source across the bonfire sprite, with edge sparks fading sooner and central sparks rising a bit higher so the plume reads as a subtle right-side-up taper without becoming exaggerated.
note.summary: Campfire motes should taper upward from the fire bed

note.details: Blink preview suppresses generic path_tiles markers and draws assets/art/effects/blink_rift_preview.png as a single transformed rift mark, with vector ribbon only as a load-failure fallback. Preserve this direction for future polish so the preview does not expose circles, arcs, fray strokes, or other obvious construction primitives.
note.summary: Blink preview rift uses one textured smoke strip

note.details: Trap damage is intentionally tuned above weak direct ranged attacks: first-sequence local depths deal 6/7/8 player-scale damage, boss-depth traps deal 9, and later sequences add 2 per completed sequence. Status payloads still use local encounter depth so early fire/poison traps keep shallow pressure.
note.summary: Generated traps are a high-value positional payoff

note.details: Trap damage is intentionally tuned above weak direct ranged attacks: first-sequence standard depths deal 6/7/8 player-scale damage, first-sequence boss-depth traps deal 5 to avoid one-shotting full-health lightning wisps, and later sequences add 2 per completed sequence. Status payloads still use local encounter depth so early fire/poison traps keep shallow pressure.
note.summary: Generated traps are a high-value positional payoff

note.details: For selected card hover previews, apply the hovered target through _card_preview_from_state and call finish_player_card when that preview is complete before forecasting pass damage. Otherwise card time/hand removal/card-play counters are omitted and turn order can look safer than the click-confirmed result.
note.summary: Pass preview hover must include selected-card commit when confirmation completes the card.

note.details: The run HUD's top-left TitleBox should show the room name prominently with only a Depth N subtitle below it. Do not reintroduce element labels, turn number, card-play counts, or other combat metadata into that corner unless the design is explicitly revisited.
note.summary: Top-left room header should stay terse

note.details: CombatBoardView draws assets/art/tiles/campfire_bonfire.png and campfire_bonfire_idle.png directly; no runtime alpha cleanup is applied to the campfire prop, and no unaltered animation source is checked in. Future repairs should use frame-local exterior flood-fill to preserve border-connected transparency while filling only enclosed low-alpha islands inside the flame/smoke artwork.
note.summary: Campfire bonfire alpha cleanup is baked into PNG assets

note.details: campfire_bonfire_idle.png is rebuilt from the user-redownloaded 4096x3840 transparent source sheet by cropping each 1024x960 cell to its shared 992x640 alpha bbox, then filling only enclosed low-alpha islands inside the flame/smoke. campfire_bonfire.png uses the first rebuilt frame as the static fallback. Do not run broad alpha cleanup across the stone-circle interior; preserve border-connected transparency and only repair enclosed transparent holes.
note.summary: Campfire bonfire assets come from the redownloaded transparent sheet

note.details: Enemy definitions can declare death_spawn={type=split, enemy_type, count, radius, summoned}. CombatEngine skips death_spawn for summoned parents and marks split children summoned by default, so reward/card-play suppression and no-resplit behavior stay centralized.
note.summary: Enemy split-on-death uses death_spawn data hooks

note.details: For new enemy sprites, match the existing roster's board-scale language: broad dark-fantasy silhouettes, readable head/body proportions, muted painterly surfaces, and one clear accent. Avoid concept-art sprites with tiny heads, micro-armor details, or tall detailed figures scaled down to the same height as the player.
note.summary: Enemy sprites should use chunky readable painterly silhouettes

note.details: Avoid full-opaque, full-bleed generated item art for Scavenger consumables. Generate/source the subject, then composite through existing card-art alpha masks and verify in CardWidget so the art stays inside the card frame.
note.summary: Consumable item card art should use the same ragged transparent art-window treatment as normal cards.

note.details: For merchants such as the Scavenger, avoid highly detailed or realistic generated sprites. Crop to a readable silhouette, simplify/pixel-cluster the result, and compare against blacksmith/arcanist/player/enemy sheets before installing.
note.summary: NPC merchant sprites should stay chunky and low-detail, matching player/enemy sprite density.

note.details: For large non-combat selection prompts such as GROW YOUR POWER and CLAIM YOUR TREASURE, avoid simple geometric halos, underlines, sweep parallelograms, or other obvious decorative shapes behind the text. Keep depth/life treatments tied to the letterforms themselves: text-shaped shadow, glow, bevel/highlight, or similarly professional glyph-based effects.
note.summary: Selection prompt depth effects should be glyph-shaped

note.details: Character Gear item cards should use cropped art icons, not two-letter text badges, and player-facing equip/stow controls should stay drag-based like equipment. Dragging an equipped consumable back to inventory may leave the item loadout empty; do not reintroduce button-only item management unless the interaction model is deliberately redesigned.
note.summary: Item loadout UI should mirror gear drag/drop

note.details: The initial torch ember tuning of 3 very tiny low-alpha motes was too hard to see at board scale. Prefer a slightly brighter, four-mote-per-torch treatment that remains small and sparse but catches the eye without becoming ambient room fire particles.
note.summary: Column torch embers should be subtle but readable

note.details: The July 2026 Retro Diffusion Advanced Animations -> Idle flow produced 16-frame PNG sheets at 1020x1020 total for 255x255 unit art, i.e. 4x4 cells at native 255x255 frame size. Configure these sheets with idle_sheet_columns:4, idle_sheet_rows:4, idle_sheet_order:row_major, idle_sheet_ping_pong:false. Older placeholder/anime trial idle sheets may be 4080px-wide 4x-upscaled sheets with different ping-pong metadata, so do not infer one convention from the other.
note.summary: Retro Diffusion advanced idle sheets use native 4x4 cells

note.details: Retro Diffusion 255px idle frames can produce opaque bounds but non-triangulatable silhouette polygons at the broad UNIT_SHADOW_SIMPLIFY_EPSILON=3.0 pass, which makes _draw_unit_shadow fall back to the old oval for those frames. Keep the finer retry path in _unit_shadow_data_for_texture before using an oval fallback.
note.summary: Unit shadow simplification can drop generated idle frames

note.details: The title face is implemented with fine clipped Label bands under TitleFaceBlend. A ShaderMaterial using FRAGCOORD produced a smooth fill in code but visual probes on macOS display scaling made most of the title render too dark, so future title-face polish should prefer the clipped-label ramp unless the shader can use stable local text coordinates.
note.summary: Main menu title gradient avoids screen-space shaders

note.details: The smooth title face is rendered by a single TitleFaceGradient Label with a CanvasItem shader that passes VERTEX.y from vertex() to fragment() and samples the vertical color ramp from local label coordinates. The earlier FRAGCOORD screen-space shader went too dark under macOS display scaling, while clipped-label bands remained visibly striped; prefer the local-coordinate shader for future title-face polish.
note.summary: Main menu title face uses a local-coordinate shader

note.details: CombatEngine assigns enemy intents from the enemy definition plus depth/sequence scaling only; room_element no longer converts generic attacks into fire/ice/lightning/air/earth variants. RoomGenerator gates specialist normal-room pools by matching room element: cinder_ooze=fire, frostglass_lancer=ice, chainbound_gaoler=air, bile_bloomer=earth; cinder_droplet remains split-only.
note.summary: Enemy room elements now gate specialists instead of rewriting generic attacks

reason: Fire trap shallow-burn tuning remains, but it no longer matches a combat-engine fire enemy burn ramp because enemy room-element attack rewriting was removed.

note.details: RunScene simulates move_to_room on a duplicated room-mode run state to build the pre-battle enemy/deck/loadout preview without sealing or moving rooms. The Start button calls _on_map_view_room_selected with skip_pre_battle=true to use the normal transition/analytics path, and the preview stays below the character overlay so equipment or magic swaps can update the preview before combat starts.
note.summary: Combat room entry now pauses on a visual pre-battle preview

note.details: Combat-room selection should move the run into mode=pre_battle at the destination before showing enemy details. The overlay has no back/close affordance and Start calls RunEngine.begin_pre_battle_combat so equipment, magic, and item loadout changes made in pre_battle rebuild the actual opening combat from the current deck. Do not restore the earlier behavior that previewed enemies before moving into the room.
note.summary: Pre-battle combat preview is a committed room mode, not a scouting modal

note.details: The pre-battle preview scrim is a full-screen input blocker. When Equip opens the character/loadout overlay from pre-battle, keep the preview visible behind it but set the pre-battle scrim mouse_filter to IGNORE and move the character overlay to front; restore STOP when the character overlay closes.
note.summary: Pre-battle scrim must release mouse input while character overlay is open

note.details: When an enemy dies after forced movement or a trap, before_state may contain the pre-push tile while after_state still carries the defeated enemy at the actual death tile. Death hold/dissolve units should source pos/footprint from after_enemy when available, falling back to before_enemy only when the defeated enemy was removed.
note.summary: Death animation presentation should use the enemy's final after-state position.

note.details: Room equipment drops intentionally render larger and raised above the tile with a warm pickup glow blended with rarity accent; pure rarity tint made common grey gear blend back into cinder floors.
note.summary: Equipment pickups use a warm visibility beacon

note.details: After inspection feedback, avoid glowing oval/ground-puddle treatments under equipment loot. Keep the cue as a stronger pulsing isometric tile diamond plus the actual equipment icon bobbing above its grounded shadow; this preserves visibility without making the floor effect look like a separate object.
note.summary: Equipment pickups use tile pulses and bobbing, not oval glows

note.details: Card rarity values now use the same four-tier set as relics and equipment: common, rare, epic, legendary. Starting cards should use starter: true plus a normal rarity, usually common; do not use starter as a rarity value. GameData/CardWidget still normalize legacy uncommon to rare and legacy starter to common for compatibility.
note.summary: Cards now use shared loot rarity tiers

note.details: Standard combat local depths 1-3 share the normal enemy roster; depth controls density and stat scaling. Generic enemies can appear at any standard depth, matching elemental specialists can appear from depth one, and boss-only/split-only enemies remain excluded from normal pools.
note.summary: Normal-room enemy roster eligibility is no longer depth-gated

note.details: SteamService initializes GodotSteam before menu/run scenes load, runs callbacks, and when a logged-in Steam user is active sets custom_user_dir_name to Escape the Umbra/steam/<64-bit SteamID> unless a parallel task namespace is already active. Steam Auto-Cloud should use the matching Escape the Umbra/steam/{64BitSteamID} subdirectory and sync progression.json plus current_run.save only; keep user://analytics local by default because it is append-only balancing telemetry.
note.summary: Steam runtime uses account-scoped Godot user data

note.details: For elemental-intensity CardWidget glow, use show_behind_parent with relative z_index 0 rather than z_index -1. HandFanContainer assigns the first card slot z_index 0, so a negative child z can place the first card's glow below the hand/background plane until hover/focus lifts the widget. Keeping the glow at the card z-plane lets later hand cards cover it while preserving visibility for the first card.
note.summary: Active card glow must stay at card z-plane

note.details: Victory banking and defeat loss processing clear run_state.held_embers before later UI refreshes. Preserve the terminal amount in dedicated presentation state and build the recap from committed progression plus that captured amount; recomputing from the ended run will incorrectly show zero and can misreport recovery-marker consequences.
note.summary: Run-end recap values must be captured before terminal state clearing

note.details: Keep prompt definitions and trigger priority in ContextualCombatTutorial, keep presentation in ContextualCombatPrompt, and integrate RunScene only through combat context plus interaction completion hooks. Prompt state persists under combat_micro_prompt_states; the layout host belongs above the hand so prompts never cover board targets or HUD anchors.
note.summary: Combat onboarding uses five first-run contextual micro-prompts

note.details: RunScene holds the newest coherent run snapshot separately while card, room-travel, and enemy animations render local before/after states; _committed_run_state and close paths must prefer that hold so animation-time quits cannot roll back. CombatEngine commit steps belong before each enemy mutation's presentation and must carry the post-action rng_state plus initiative/turn checkpoints. Never serialize hover, selection, drag, or animation presentation state.
note.summary: Committed saves stay ahead of combat presentation

note.details: The committed pre-battle overlay groups duplicate card ids into xN tiles and switches to the 120px three-column dense layout at nine groups (attuned magic is always dense). This keeps the 19-card maximum immediately visible without a deck scrollbar at 1280x720 and larger; retain the auto ScrollContainer only for genuinely extreme overflow.
note.summary: Pre-battle Active Deck uses counted dense tiles at supported sizes

note.details: Player-facing command/action Buttons and OptionButtons should use UiSkin compact, standard, large, destructive, selected, or icon StyleBoxFlat variants plus the non-interactive themed ornament. Do not reintroduce stretched per-state bitmap buttons. Card widgets and parchment navigation lists are intentional non-command exceptions. Styling must preserve existing focus modes, neighbors, controller traversal, and bindings.
note.summary: Command buttons use scalable UiSkin variants, not state bitmaps

note.details: A pass or enemy-action checkpoint is not resumable merely because its dictionary is coherent: empty/transition and enemy actors cannot accept player input, and replaying CombatEngine would duplicate actions, counters, status ticks, or RNG. Persist a bounded pending_combat_checkpoints cursor of already-resolved full combat snapshots, consume/save those snapshots in order after load, and retain an explicit transition actor so legacy saves that omit current_actor can still default safely to a player turn.
note.summary: Mid-enemy saves require snapshot continuations

note.details: Terminal commit paths must pass their terminal dictionary through this state-in/state-out helper, adopt the embedded progression before ember banking/loss and save_data, and only then set processed flags. The bounded completed-result ledger preserves the original stats and NEW BEST decision for non-adjacent replay; UI-only victory/defeat hooks are not a durable save boundary.
note.summary: Record run results through the supplied terminal state before persistence

note.details: The committed-boundary save path can finalize and clear victory/defeat before the later recap hooks run. _finalize_terminal_committed_state must call _terminal_state_with_recorded_run_result first and adopt its embedded progression before banking/loss processing and save_data; the durable result ledger makes reload retries idempotent.
note.summary: Record run results inside terminal checkpoint finalization

reason: Redundant with the existing terminal-state persistence decision.

note.details: Do not put a mandatory mode-choice click between selecting a card and using its printed action. A click should immediately enter normal printed targeting while a persistent mode-tab row defaults to CARD; optional fallback tabs may retarget the same card and must display their live values, such as ATTACK 20 and MOVE 2, with unavailable modes visibly disabled.
note.summary: Clicked combat cards default directly to their printed action

note.details: A clicked card immediately enters its printed action. PRINTED, ATTACK 20, and MOVE 2 must be presented as one mutually exclusive radio-style mode selector, not navigation tabs: exactly one selected option uses a filled indicator and strong fill; available unselected options stay bright; unavailable options are substantially dimmed and desaturated. Keep the live fallback values visible and do not squeeze neighboring labels to fit.
note.summary: Combat card alternatives use an exclusive mode selector

note.details: Card previews/options, shortcut plans, and pass forecasts cache only within an unchanged combat-state/selection revision; state replacement and selection progression must call the corresponding mark/invalidate helper. Direct test-state assignment is covered by state hashes. Optimized move legality, AOE target lookup, movement plans, and shortcut prefilters retain exhaustive-reference equality checks in the performance harnesses.
note.summary: Combat preview caches are revision-scoped and semantics-tested

note.details: RunScene may pass combat/presentation dictionaries by reference because CombatBoardView never mutates them. The view keeps a deep snapshot only of derived-cache inputs to detect later in-place changes, indexes per-tile render data, lazily loads only submitted unit types, and renders invariant background/floors on the parent while its internal dynamic layer handles previews, units, particles, and animation. Preserve the static/dynamic draw-order equivalence and mutation-detection tests when changing submissions.
note.summary: CombatBoardView uses read-only borrowed snapshots and retained static rendering

note.details: A reused CardWidget child under CardProxy can silently double from 250x352 to 500x704 when FULL_RECT anchors resolve again during configure, even while the proxy scale itself reports the correct value. Keep the CardWidget at fixed native top-left geometry, reapply _prepare_native_card_widget after configure/display overrides, and let the proxy parent own all drag/play/draw/discard scaling. Visual probes should assert the child widget size across multiple pool reuse cycles, not only the proxy scale.
note.summary: Pooled card proxy widgets must clear stretch anchors after configure

note.details: Played cards should use one persistent proxy from hand through a modest grow into center, a readable hold, and a smooth shrinking flight into the destination pile; do not fade/release and respawn between those legs. Play, draw, discard, consume, and snapback should favor continuous zero-speed-endpoint easing over segmented Back-eased tweens. Multi-card draws should overlap with a short stagger and remain in their fan slots until the authoritative hand refresh replaces them.
note.summary: Card motion should be continuous, readable, and physically staged

note.details: A played card should use one persistent proxy, grow modestly into center for only a short identification beat, then complete its shrink-and-pile flight before any card action animation starts so it never covers movement, damage, block, or other resolution visuals. Keep the full pre-action cadence quick. Multi-card draws should remain smooth and overlapping but launch as a readable stream with enough stagger to perceive one card, then the next, rather than appearing simultaneous.
note.summary: Card motion should be continuous, brief, and action-first

note.details: RunEngine.finish_combat must resolve every unclaimed equipment loot entry into claimed/resolution=missed and carry missed_equipment ids before combat_state is cleared. RunScene may retain the pre-resolution victory snapshot only long enough to animate the cinder disintegration, then transitions with the resolved snapshot for analytics and persistence. Grimoire discovery for floor equipment begins on collection, not mere visibility, so missed gear never becomes discovered.
note.summary: Victory resolves missed equipment before clearing combat

note.details: Keep the combat log as a larger high-contrast framed panel with body-large outlined text; missed-equipment disintegration copy belongs only in the combat log, not the action banner.
note.summary: Combat log should be prominent and own missed-gear copy

note.details: New equipment/items append to unread_loadout_equipment and new reward/merchant spells append to unread_loadout_magic. RunScene derives both the header count and Gear/Magic tab badges from these arrays, and clears only the category whose character tab was opened so save/resume and mixed acquisitions stay honest.
note.summary: Loadout notifications use per-category durable unread ids

note.details: Cards with top-level flurry:true expand their printed actions once per card play available when the printed play begins. The commit spends that snapshotted count and multiplies printed time and health cost by it; card-play bonuses or kill refunds earned during repeated actions are not folded back into the repeat count and remain available afterward. Fallback Attack/Move modes do not inherit Flurry.
note.summary: Flurry snapshots card plays before resolution

note.details: Acquired equipment, consumable items, and magic ids are recorded in both unread_loadout_* for the top-bar/tab notification and new_loadout_* for item-level NEW tags. Opening Gear or Magic clears only its navigation unread list; hovering the specific asset clears and persists only that asset's NEW state, so the panel can guide the eye after its tab badge has already been acknowledged.
note.summary: Loadout discovery uses separate navigation and per-asset states

note.details: Cards with top-level flurry:true snapshot all currently available card plays, expand their printed actions once per snapped play, multiply health cost per copy, discard one physical card, and pay the top-level Time cost only once. The commit spends the snapshotted plays; bonuses or kill refunds created during resolution remain afterward. Fallback Attack/Move modes do not inherit Flurry.
note.summary: Flurry repeats effects but pays Time once

note.details: Keep Flurry's individual printed action package deliberately weak and showcase flexible hybrid utility rather than an attack-only cycle. Useful roles include block plus attack, elemental intensity plus attack, draw plus attack, and movement plus attack; the copied two-play result and single-card/single-Time compression are the payoff.
note.summary: Flurry cards earn value from copies, not printed rate

note.details: Do not overcorrect Flurry by making each printed package anemic. Keep each repeat below the rate of a normal standalone card, but tune the baseline two-copy result into the premium build-around band; the July 2026 midpoint pass landed the five payoffs around 4.6-5.7. Card-play enablers may be strong enough to make the setup exciting, including Gathering Rhythm granting 2 plays.
note.summary: Flurry cards should be modest per copy but premium in total

note.details: Avoid upright fans or stacks of three complete cards because Draw already uses that silhouette. Prefer a single large landscape card moving sideways with compact afterimage trails, while preserving the dark-fantasy parchment, ink, crimson, and gold icon style and checking it at native CardWidget size.
note.summary: Flurry icon must not resemble the Draw stack

note.details: Filtering only enemy sprites is insufficient. Hidden enemies must also be removed from direct targets and threat previews; anonymized in initiative, logs, intent/action animation banners, pass-risk forecasts, and floating combat text; and ignored during movement planning until collision. Preserve visible outcomes without leaking hidden identity, position, intent, or damage forecasts.
note.summary: Umbra hiding must cover every player-facing information surface

note.details: Section 1 is Clear, followed by Fringe, Advancing, Pressing, Deep, then Heart for the Shadow Dragon section. Eclipse is reserved for authored final encounters. Current four-depth sections are only the adapter; preserve the section mapping if boss intervals are compressed.
note.summary: Umbra pressure advances by elemental-dragon section, not absolute room count

note.details: Illuminate creates ranged circular light sources, Vision extends the player's Manhattan radius, Truesight reveals enemies without lighting tiles, and Dispel reduces the effective stage. Duration -1 is persistent; positive durations tick on the player's next activation.
note.summary: Radiance effects share activation-based Umbra duration semantics

note.details: Speculative hover, risk, shortcut, and continuation previews must never resolve hidden collision or visibility. If a multi-step movement card reveals new Umbra information after click, lock cancellation and card switching until its remaining actions resolve or are skipped; Illuminate-and-attack cards reuse the clicked light target and commit without a second cancellable reveal step.
note.summary: Umbra discovery must occur only after an irreversible choice

note.details: Umbra should shade the board atmosphere while character sprites, props, and equipment pickups remain crisp in the foreground. Present its stage as a dedicated room-header line such as 'Deep Umbra'; the elemental intensity HUD remains five elements only.
note.summary: Render Umbra behind board objects and label it separately from elemental intensity

note.details: CombatBoardView custom drawing is not clipped by the board Control's own clip_contents setting. Keep Backdrop/Margin/MainVBox/StageRoot.clip_contents enabled so zoomed or panned tiles cannot paint over the top HUD or hand; the board's clip_contents still clips its dynamic child layer.
note.summary: StageRoot must clip the navigable combat board

note.details: Active temporary light sources need persistent on-board markers with duration counters; True Sight needs a player-HUD badge, counter, and tooltip; expired light should let fog visibly creep back over about one second; and Umbra action icons should favor bold small-size silhouettes over detailed art.
note.summary: Umbra effects must remain legible during combat

note.details: Board zoom and pan must not trigger contextual combat prompt relayout. The note is fixed HUD information; navigation_changed should remain a board signal but should not be connected to prompt placement.
note.summary: Combat notes stay fixed while the board moves

note.details: The navigable board must remain unclipped so its art can flow beneath the bottom controls. Keep the board and base backdrop in BoardUnderlay below UiLayer, align the board's interactive rect to StageRoot, and leave broad UI layout controls mouse-filtered to IGNORE so input still reaches the board.
note.summary: Combat board renders on a HUD underlay canvas

note.details: The approved direction is a 112x64 transparent timeline: two crimson outline card echoes progress along a gold baseline into one fully rendered parchment card. CardWidget gives the Flurry token about 1.8x normal width but only 1.05x normal height; doubling a square slot made the following row gaps visibly too large. Keep it distinct from Draw's upright stacked-card silhouette and validate at native 250x352 card size.
note.summary: Flurry uses a wide timeline icon with a shallow card-row slot

note.details: Keep depth 1 Clear, then use Fringe on first-section depths 2 and 3 and retain Fringe for the depth-4 boss. Later section stages remain Fringe, Advancing, Pressing, Deep, and Heart rather than shifting the entire curve forward. The card heuristic uses 0.75 Umbra relevance because only the first depth is guaranteed Clear.
note.summary: Introduce Fringe Umbra before the first elemental dragon

note.details: Radiance cards unlock the shared Radiance/effect articles, but their card pages follow their source taxonomy. Reward or attuned Radiance cards use Magicks; equipment-only Radiance cards such as Lantern Shot receive a card-preview entry under the granting equipment slot instead of being mislabeled as Magicks.
note.summary: Radiance does not determine Grimoire card provenance

note.details: When multiple card actions use reuse_previous_target, render their icons on the same logical and physical line because a new line communicates a new target choice. Keep automatic non-target effects on their own rows as needed, and avoid wrapping a shared-target row into apparent extra target lines. Matching range tokens within the shared target group should be shown once.
note.summary: One card action line represents one target selection

note.details: Setting the RunScene root Control invisible does not suppress children moved under BoardUnderlay or UiLayer CanvasLayers. Isolated card-art probes that instantiate RunScene for helper methods must explicitly hide nested CanvasLayer nodes, or startup UI can cover the proof while image-dimension checks still pass.
note.summary: Hidden RunScene probes must also hide nested CanvasLayers

note.details: The fixed 940x290 merchant panel can fully hide and intercept lower board exits even though RunEngine.available_moves and map travel remain correct. Keep an explicit Show Doors collapse action with a non-blocking Return to Shop control, Escape support, and merchant_room_probe coverage that clicks a formerly covered door at a 1280x720 logical viewport.
note.summary: Merchant trade overlays can cover legal doors at 1280x720

note.details: For normal card targeting and the Printed/Attack/Move choice, place the card title and step count directly above the exclusive mode selector. Do not show the action-type line or the target-validity/turn-end-risk line; keep drag-only release guidance because it communicates the distinct drag gesture.
note.summary: Card action context should omit redundant metadata rows

note.details: For normal card targeting and the Printed/Attack/Move choice, place the card title and step count directly above the exclusive mode selector without action-type or target-validity/turn-end-risk rows. Position the contextual widget directly above and horizontally aligned with the active hand card so it reads as part of the card interaction; retain drag-only release guidance.
note.summary: Card action context stays compact and anchored to the active card

note.details: Keep every concealed tile clearly darkened for tactical readability, then layer coherent rounded violet-black cloud lobes with visible slow drift. Boundary contours should stay thin and subordinate; avoid long narrow ribbons or zig-zag bands that make the effect look like linework.
note.summary: Umbra should read as filled, billowing tile shadow

note.details: Merchant panel content is taller than the generic 248px relic-choice host; centering oversized content can clip the panel bottom at 1280x720 and leave it unsafe near laptop/full-HD viewport edges. Size the host from _relic_choice_bar.get_combined_minimum_size().y, keep the merchant control labeled Hide with Return to Shop and Escape as reversible access, and cover fresh 720p and 1080p launches in merchant_room_probe.
note.summary: Merchant trade overlay must size its host to real content

note.details: For normal card targeting and the Printed/Attack/Move choice, omit action-type and target-validity/turn-end-risk rows. Position the contextual widget directly above the active hand card. When play commits, lock the widget's exact screen position through card-flight and action-resolution animations so hand rebuilding or reflow cannot shift it; retain drag-only release guidance.
note.summary: Card action context stays compact, card-anchored, and motion-stable

note.details: RunScene combat HUDs, fanned hand cards, and transient effects use positive or absolute z-index values up to the 1600s. A modal scrim left at z=0 will dim only lower siblings while cards and turn/pass widgets render over it. Keep MenuScrim z_as_relative=false above gameplay surfaces; both the pause dialog and in-run SettingsPanel stay descendants of that scrim.
note.summary: Pause and settings scrim must use an absolute top gameplay z-order

note.details: Zero-HP terrain is hidden by normal board drawing, so RunScene diffs before/after terrain state, holds destruction frame 0 during impact/floating-text presentation, then supplies presentation-only terrain_destruction_units through the animation. Tile-scoped damage sources such as player/enemy AOE, deterministic lightning strikes, and trap blasts should apply the same damage to destructible terrain on every affected tile.
note.summary: Terrain destruction presentation is transition-driven

note.details: For move-plus-attack intents, prefer the shortest safe path to the first attack-enabling endpoint; move_away may maximize separation only while preserving the attack. If no same-turn attack exists, future routing gives finite costs to destructible terrain and allied congestion and a high finite cost to traps. Resolution keeps the selected target for the full activation, and exact path data is reused by animation and hover projections.
note.summary: Enemy activations use one deterministic target and route plan for movement, attack, preview, and analytics.

note.details: Targeted move-plus-attack intents minimize movement to an attack-enabling endpoint first, then prefer safer equal-length paths; move-away attacks preserve the attack, while attackless retreats maximize safe separation. Future routing uses finite terrain-clearing and trap costs, treats allies as hard current but temporary future blockers, and credits an immediately traversable prefix to avoid needless stalls. Exact hover projections reuse the plan and honor freeze, shock, immobilize, and deterministic lightning tiles.
note.summary: Enemy activations share one deterministic plan across resolution, preview, animation, and analytics.

note.details: On enemy death, do not play the ember-collect sample or launch board-traveling currency motes. Combine simultaneous kill rewards into one exact counter gain, roll the header count in about 0.2 seconds, and limit flair to a restrained warm pulse plus a terse +N beside the counter; reduced-motion should remain supported.
note.summary: Enemy ember gains should be quiet, brief, and header-local

note.details: The preferred movement preview is a very thick cyan route ribbon occupying more than half the projected tile height, with one proportionately large classic destination head. Preserve blended highlight and bevel layers plus a visibly offset cast shadow so it reads above the board; avoid thin linework, tiny repeated segment heads, and waypoint-dot styling.
note.summary: Movement paths should use fat elevated arrow ribbons

note.details: Inspection feedback refined the initial fat-arrow direction: keep the shaft near half the projected tile height after outline/glow, use smoothly interpolated shading instead of visible color bands, and form the large terminal head as an open-backed continuation of the shaft so no rear outline or rounded cap creates a pasted-on seam, especially after turns.
note.summary: Movement arrows should be half-tile blended ribbons with seamless heads

note.details: Keep the half-tile blended ribbon and seamless open-backed head, with the cyan face slightly translucent so board texture remains faintly visible while the outline and shadow stay crisp. When building translucency from layered strokes, keep each highlight layer low-alpha and avoid repeated waypoint discs, which accumulate into visible circular blotches.
note.summary: Movement arrows should be subtly translucent half-tile ribbons

note.details: The preferred movement arrow is a subtly translucent ribbon around 0.41 projected tile height with a proportionately scaled 0.50-tile head. Merge shaft and head geometry into one polygon before drawing shadow, outline, translucency, and gradient layers; even an open-backed separately shaded head reads glued on or askew. Preserve the shared perspective and avoid internal join boundaries or repeated waypoint-disc overdraw.
note.summary: Movement arrow heads must share one silhouette and depth treatment with the shaft

note.details: The approved direction after the 0.41/0.50 pass is a roughly 0.37 projected-tile-height shaft with a 0.45-tile-wide symmetric triangular head. Keep the head and shaft merged before all rendering, use straight rear shoulders or subtly concave shaft joins rather than convex flares, and carry one clipped directional light sweep across the unified silhouette so the head shares the tail's face plane. Render the raised arrow over traps and ordinary ground loot, but under units and floating equipment pickups.
note.summary: Movement arrows use a symmetric triangular head and explicit floor-item layering

note.details: Keep the approved roughly 0.37 shaft/0.45 head silhouette, seamless union, clipped lighting, and item layering, but construct the head's rear shoulder edge along the board's other isometric grid axis rather than a Euclidean screen-space perpendicular. Place the head so its base just crosses the destination tile's near edge and its tip ends clearly inside that tile (current reach ratios 0.29 back and 0.18 forward), making the route read as landing on the highlighted square rather than pointing to the next one.
note.summary: Movement arrow heads follow isometric grid perspective and straddle the landing tile edge

note.details: The five gear slots plus item slots exceed the fixed character body at supported viewports. Leaving that column unscrolled raises the shared HBox minimum height, so every Gear subpanel extends beneath CharacterBodyFrame and is clipped. Keep the outer dialog/tab bounds fixed and contain the loadout list in its own vertical ScrollContainer.
note.summary: Character Gear loadout must scroll inside the fixed body

note.details: Keep the seamless isometric silhouette, translucent gradient, outline, and shadow. Current approved direction uses shaft ratio 0.333, head width 0.405, tip reach 0.138, and tail reach 0.285; player paths are cyan, enemy intent/move paths are purple, ground items stay below the path, and units/floating equipment stay above it.
note.summary: Movement paths use slim dimensional unified arrows with shared cyan/purple geometry

note.details: The game enables project-wide 4x 2D MSAA. Godot's --headless dummy renderer cannot render or validate MSAA, so visual_probe_runner reads project.godot and automatically selects a native display renderer when MSAA is enabled (Metal/Mobile on macOS), or emits a clear capability error when no display is available. Non-MSAA projects retain the previous headless default.
note.summary: MSAA visual probes require an automatic GPU-backed renderer

note.details: CursorFeedback hides the native pointer and maps Control cursor shapes plus cursor_feedback_context/cursor_feedback_drag_source metadata into forged idle, action, press, drag, invalid, and loading states. New custom click/drag controls should expose those semantics instead of drawing their own cursor. Scene changes from MainMenu and RunScene route through CursorFeedback.change_scene_to_file so the loading ward renders before and just after synchronous transitions; click sounds are procedural PCM on the SFX bus.
note.summary: Global cursor feedback is semantic and autoload-owned

note.details: CursorFeedback owns the hidden native pointer, forged cursor states, procedural SFX-bus click sounds, and scene-transition loading ward. CURSOR_HELP is hover information only and must produce dull click feedback; custom point-dependent actions should expose cursor_feedback_context_at(local_position), while dynamically guarded Controls can provide a Callable in cursor_feedback_context_provider. cursor_feedback_context/cursor_feedback_drag_source remain appropriate for static action and drag semantics. Keep provider guards identical to the actual input handler guards.
note.summary: Global cursor feedback separates hover help from actual click validity

note.details: Turn-order portraits are intentionally tighter crops and can omit parts of enemies (notably Zekarion). Pre-battle summary/detail frames should prefer each enemy art_path with keep-aspect-centered fitting; turn-order UI keeps its separate portrait mapping.
note.summary: Pre-battle enemy frames use complete static combat art

note.details: In Godot 4.6, returning null from _make_custom_tooltip can fall back to raw tooltip text and Viewport.cancel_tooltip is not GDScript-bound. The focused inspection therefore clears/restores every pre-battle source tooltip, returns an invisible custom tooltip while modal, removes TooltipPanel windows, and refreshes hover ownership.
note.summary: Focused pre-battle inspections must suppress tooltip sources and retire existing tooltip popups

note.details: Cursor states should deform, tilt, trail, or recolor the same physical pointer. A press compresses toward its fixed hotspot and stays compressed while held; release produces a brief rebound. Loading animation belongs inside the heel bearing. Native suppression uses hidden mode plus transparent fallbacks for every system cursor shape.
note.summary: Custom cursor uses one reactive forged silhouette, never context glyphs

note.details: CURSOR_HELP is informational and produces dull click feedback. Point-dependent actions expose cursor_feedback_context_at(local_position); dynamically guarded Controls use cursor_feedback_context_provider with guards matching their real input handlers. Static targets may use cursor_feedback_context and cursor_feedback_drag_source. CursorFeedback owns exact-once procedural click sounds and scene-transition loading feedback.
note.summary: Cursor feedback classifies real activation separately from hover help

note.details: Bring the pinned scrim to the front when opening, suppress and restore source tooltips, and reject enemy/card/equipment click handlers while focused. RunScene receives modal mouse positions before viewport stretch while Control global rects are in stretched canvas space, so X hit testing must apply Viewport.get_final_transform() before comparing coordinates; all non-X mouse buttons stay handled by the enemy modal.
note.summary: Focused pre-battle enemy inspections must own hover and pointer input

note.details: Keep the cursor as one forged object. Build the blade from broad joined facets and edge bevels, with no bright stripe down its center. The handle bearing belongs inside a connected throat bracket, wrapped grip, angular pommel housing, bearing race, and inset socket. Avoid tiny spoke or highlight arrangements that can read as faces, letters, or action symbols. Loading may animate a single sweep around the housed bearing.
note.summary: Cursor ornament must read as joined metalwork, never an accidental glyph

note.details: Keep one coherent silhouette: presses compress toward the fixed hotspot and stay held until a brief release rebound; drags deform directionally. Build the blade from broad joined facets and edge bevels with no bright center stripe. House the loading bearing inside a connected throat bracket, wrapped grip, angular pommel, bearing race, and inset socket; use a single loading sweep. Avoid marks that resemble faces, letters, or action glyphs. Native suppression remains hidden mode plus transparent fallbacks for every system shape.
note.summary: Custom cursor is one reactive forged mechanism without symbolic ornament

note.details: Keep one coherent forged silhouette with broad blade facets, housed pommel bearing, held compression, release rebound, and directional drag deformation. A valid press must not introduce a detached white tip glint, sparkle, glyph, or other overlay; motion and material changes provide the feedback. Loading alone may use a single sweep inside the bearing.
note.summary: Custom cursor reacts through its forged body without press-only ornament

note.details: Keep the valid sound short and transient-led: high-frequency contact texture plus a close latch snap, with no low pitched body or ringing tail that reads as a boop. The inert sound remains the longer dull cinder knock. Preserve exact-once semantic classification and route both through the SFX bus.
note.summary: Valid cursor feedback is a dry mechanical click, not a tonal confirmation

note.details: RunScene native macOS mouse events already arrive in the canvas coordinates used by Control.get_global_rect(), while Input.parse_input_event replay may arrive in window coordinates and require Viewport.get_final_transform(). Modal hit tests that support both native play and injected probes must check the event position directly before checking the transformed position.
note.summary: Native and injected Godot pointer events use different coordinates

note.details: RunScene native macOS mouse events already match Control.get_global_rect() canvas coordinates. Do not also compare Viewport.get_final_transform() * event.position in production: that creates an inverse-transformed second live hit region where unrelated clicks can close the modal. Tests and replay that synthesize canvas coordinates should route them with Viewport.push_input(event, true).
note.summary: Modal hit tests must use one canvas coordinate space

note.details: When a focused pre-battle enemy inspection is open, the full-screen pinned-tooltip scrim consumes every background click without dismissal. Its cursor_feedback_context_provider must therefore return action only over the live X close-button rect and inert everywhere else; retaining the generic pinned-overlay outside-click action context produces a valid cursor/click sound for an action that will never occur.
note.summary: Modal cursor feedback must mirror suppressed input

note.details: Editable source lives in marketing/trailer; tools/steam_trailer_capture.gd produces route, prebattle, real CombatEngine trap/AoE/Umbra beats, and reward footage. The shadow-dragon main-menu art is narrative goal imagery only, and the retired teaser is not a creative reference.
note.summary: Escape the Umbra Steam trailer uses deterministic current-game capture and Remotion source

note.details: Clicking a playable card may arm and preview its Printed mode, but a card whose preview completes without a board target must not resolve until the highlighted Play Card action in the compact card-anchored rail is pressed. Keep Printed/Attack/Move switchable before commitment; Cancel or selecting another card must not spend, resolve, or emit card-play analytics. Drag-to-board remains confirmed by its explicit drop.
note.summary: Targetless card clicks require card-anchored confirmation

note.details: Chromium FontFace.load() intermittently left @remotion/fonts delayRender handles open during long renders, including with TTF, compact WOFF, embedded data URLs, and single-worker rendering. scripts/render-title-cards.py deterministically rasterizes the finite promo copy from fonts/LabyrinthCrumble-Regular.ttf into transparent PNGs; animate those assets in Remotion and regenerate them when copy or typography changes.
note.summary: Pre-render Labyrinth Crumble trailer copy instead of loading the TTF at Remotion runtime

note.details: RunScene initially renders before a requested capture state unless it is hidden, and Remotion trimBefore/poster seeking can still expose those frames during scene transitions. tools/steam_trailer_capture.gd now keeps RunScene hidden until the requested non-start state is loaded, while capture-footage.sh applies FFmpeg trim/setpts so source frame zero is safe. Preserve both layers when adding future clips.
note.summary: Physically strip Godot Movie Maker pre-roll from every trailer edit clip.

note.details: At fixed frame rates, the ember counter's frame-quantized roll timers can outlast its pulse tween. Connecting to finished after it already fired suspends the coroutine forever and leaves RunScene's card-resolution animation lock set. Guard late awaits with is_valid() and is_running().
note.summary: Do not await Tween.finished after independent timer awaits unless the tween is still running.

note.details: A correct non-start RunEngine state does not guarantee the first visible Movie Maker frames are safe: large-map and prebattle overlays can draw several frames after their state-changing calls complete, briefly exposing the underlying room or a half-composed overlay. Keep the RunScene hidden while preparing the requested UI, physically trim each edit source past its measured stable frame, and verify a dense early-frame contact sheet plus every encoded transition. For the deterministic route/prebattle captures, capture-footage.sh currently uses raw-frame trims 27 and 56.
note.summary: Audit deferred Godot trailer UI frame-by-frame before choosing source trims

note.details: CombatBoardView emits equipment:<id> tooltip triggers and calls an injected equipment_tooltip_builder. RunScene wires _build_equipment_tooltip_panel in _ready so collectible equipment shows the same supplied-card previews as the equip menu while the board remains reusable; without a builder, the board falls back to a framed name-and-slot tooltip.
note.summary: Board equipment pickups reuse the RunScene equipment tooltip builder

note.details: For Escape the Umbra trailers, capture a real non-start engine-generated room with its walls, props, moss, loot, enemies, and legal run state. Drive cards through the production hand selection, targeting, center-stage card, discard, and resolution flow; compose camera motion around that footage instead of direct action-step shortcuts or synthetic empty grids. Light-source shots must visibly and mechanically clear real Umbra darkness, with before/after visibility assertions.
note.summary: Trailer tactical footage must preserve authentic generated rooms and production card play

note.details: DragonBossLibrary deterministically shuffles Tharokh, Vyraketh, Vaeloryx, Iskaldra, and Zekarion across depths 4/8/12/16/20 without repeats; Noctyrax is fixed at 24. Boss encounters end when the live boss_bar actor dies even if authored hazards or summoned adds remain. Boss health and mechanic payloads use global-depth sequence scaling. Boss-bar actors remain revealed through Umbra so the final boss is readable and targetable while Eclipse still punishes actors outside Radiance.
note.summary: Dragon bosses use a seeded five-gate roster before Noctyrax at depth 24

note.details: Use shot-specific pan and zoom keyframes that center the real interaction target as it moves. Avoid generic center zooms that push edge-located map traversal, reward offers, merchant rows, or equip targets into the vignette. Validate the composed edit—not only source footage—with dense frame sheets.
note.summary: Trailer camera tracks the actual UI focus

note.details: DragonBossLibrary deterministically shuffles Tharokh, Vyraketh, Vaeloryx, Iskaldra, and Zekarion across depths 4/8/12/16/20 without repeats; Noctyrax is fixed at depth 24. Noctyrax enters with two depth-scaled Veilbound Acolytes whose visibility makes Radiance and Truesight tactically relevant during Last Eclipse. Boss-bar actors remain revealed through Umbra, large-enemy direct targets enumerate and mark each legal footprint tile above the sprite, and boss health/name bars stay inside the combat board below the turn-order header. Boss encounters end when the live boss_bar actor dies even if authored hazards or adds remain.
note.summary: Dragon bosses use seeded gates; Noctyrax closes the run with visibility-focused adds

note.details: For UI choices, use one eased approach into the real option area, an intentional readable hold, a selection-timed impact, and one eased pullback. Do not apply Bezier easing separately across multi-waypoint interpolation tracks because it visibly stops and restarts. Keep the lower source edge covered, remove shading over action UI, and spend added pacing before the actual selection rather than on an empty post-choice room. Validate composed motion at dense frame cadence.
note.summary: Trailer camera uses continuous action-timed phases

note.details: Card simulations may internally move the player, change vision or Umbra, collide with concealed enemies, and trigger traps or loot. Until the card crosses the existing irreversible commit boundary, render the committed player, Umbra, traps, loot, log, and visibility while retaining safe preview data such as damage to already-visible enemies; otherwise previews disclose hidden board state before Play Card confirmation.
note.summary: Unconfirmed movement previews must preserve committed Umbra information

note.details: DragonBossLibrary deterministically shuffles Tharokh, Vyraketh, Vaeloryx, Iskaldra, and Zekarion across depths 4/8/12/16/20 without repeats; Noctyrax is fixed at depth 24. Noctyrax enters with two depth-scaled Veilbound Acolytes whose visibility makes Radiance and Truesight tactically relevant during Last Eclipse. Boss-bar actors remain revealed through Umbra. Large enemies use the established red attack glow and pulsing boundary across their full footprint when any visible footprint tile is a legal direct target; all footprint tiles click the same actor. Boss name and health layout derives clearance from the live turn-order panel. Boss encounters end when the boss-bar actor dies even if authored hazards or adds remain.
note.summary: Dragon bosses use seeded gates; Noctyrax closes the run with visibility-focused adds

note.details: RunScene board and reward UI live in CanvasLayers, so scaling the parent Control does not affect recorded pixels. For trailer relic and spell captures, mount the production RunScene in a larger 16:9 SubViewport, position the production choice host before it becomes visible, assert the selected control clears the viewport bottom safety margin, and inspect the encoded source frame before compositing.
note.summary: Reward capture must move CanvasLayer UI inside its own viewport

note.details: For Magic and Equipment loadout footage, use one restrained approach zoom, one continuous source-to-destination follow aligned to the real drag or swap, a short result hold, and one pullback. Do not use multi-waypoint pan and scale tracks that change direction or apply eased motion separately per segment. Validate at dense frame cadence.
note.summary: Trailer menu cameras follow the real swap once

note.details: DragonBossLibrary deterministically shuffles Tharokh, Vyraketh, Vaeloryx, Iskaldra, and Zekarion across depths 4/8/12/16/20 without repeats; Noctyrax is fixed at depth 24 and enters with two depth-scaled Veilbound Acolytes. Boss-bar actors remain revealed through Umbra. Large enemies use the established red attack glow and pulsing boundary across their full footprint when any visible footprint tile is a legal direct target; all footprint tiles click the same actor. Boss name, exact HP, segmented health, and damage preview live entirely inside a boss dossier that replaces the TURN CLOCK legend column without increasing the turn-order panel height or covering the board. Boss encounters end when the boss-bar actor dies even if authored hazards or adds remain.
note.summary: Dragon bosses use seeded gates; Noctyrax closes the run with visibility-focused adds

note.details: CombatBoardView derives each warm reach overlay and its perimeter from rendered tiles whose Manhattan distance to the placed source is within the source radius. Keep this presentation geometry aligned with CombatEngine.umbra_visible_tiles/_light_source_covers_tile so the lit area never promises visibility or Radiance protection that gameplay does not grant.
note.summary: Placed light visuals mirror Illuminate's Manhattan footprint

note.details: Player cards with top-level intensity_cost synthesize one required spend before printed actions; enemy actions build with type:intensity or pay attached spend_intensity costs. Trap damage is centralized in scripts/elemental_intensity_rules.gd at 72/94/124/162/208/262/324 percent for intensity 0-6, and generated traps preserve base_damage with damage fallback for older saves.
note.summary: Elemental intensity is a contested room resource with centralized scaling rules

note.details: Placed light must preserve the exact Illuminate Manhattan gameplay footprint while presenting it as overlapping blurred warm falloff with no hard tile or perimeter outline. The orb should use a feathered luminous core, close glow, gentle breathing scale/brightness, subtle bob and internal drift, while keeping the remaining-activation text readable without a framed badge.
note.summary: Placed light uses soft animated glow without construction lines

note.details: Do not add a separate bracket, corner, notch, or inward-siphon frame around intensity-spending cards; the user considers that ornament crude and unpolished. A spender whose cost is currently payable should use the existing elemental IntensityActiveGlow exactly like a satisfied intensity gate, while an unpayable spender stays unlit. Keep the negative elemental amount in the cost row as the distinction between spending and gating.
note.summary: Funded intensity spenders reuse the gated-card glow

note.details: Player base initiative is fixed at 9. Qualitative progression effects stay outside intrinsic printed-card coefficients; use the progression_skills analytics context to compare learned-skill cohorts and note exceptional interactions during review.
note.summary: Card scoring uses a fixed-initiative no-skill reference profile

note.details: Variants are extracted by flood-filling the selected component from the base floor sheet, keeping neighboring tiles transparent. CombatBoardView loads them untrimmed so every tile retains the same isometric canvas and avoids neighbor-fragment warping.
note.summary: Stone floor variants use isolated tile-only textures

note.details: Definitions can override idle sheet columns, rows, order, and frame seconds while same-stem idle loading remains automatic. The default is 4x2 row-major at 0.10 seconds; Dust Acolyte uses 2x4 column-major at 0.20 seconds, covered by focused tests.
note.summary: CombatBoardView idle animation is data-driven per unit

note.details: CombatBoardView applies art_offset_x/y after fit and scale; adjust sprite centering in enemy or NPC data instead of changing global anchoring. Introduced for the Dust Acolyte alignment and covered by the enemy art-offset test.
note.summary: Combat board unit art honors per-definition art offsets

note.details: RoomGenerator returns moss floor, wall, and pillar lists; CombatEngine and RunEngine carry them through room and combat state; CombatBoardView renders seeded overlays on stone floors and wall or pillar props. Passability and floor variants remain purely stone.
note.summary: Room moss lives in decorative metadata instead of terrain IDs

note.details: The tree uses compact stateful medallions, visible ports, and orthogonal connections inside protected graph space; full names, requirements, and effects live in the fixed detail pane so connections cannot be occluded. note.details: For profile-owned rewards such as the first-boss Moltshard, persist the award and progression_analytics_outbox entry together before append. Append only after the gameplay/outbox checkpoint succeeds, use stable run/combat idempotency keys, acknowledge separately after append, and carry terminal pending entries in the profile so crash, retry, and append-before-ack paths cannot lose or duplicate events. note.summary: Progression analytics must stage durable intent before JSONL append

note.details: Leveling grants a bankable unspent skill point. Learning one legal node commits immediately with no draft or allocation confirmation. Reset requires one Moltshard and one yes/no prompt, then immediately clears the whole tree and restores every earned point. Pointer hover may update highlights and details only: it must not grab focus, scroll the graph, recompute navigation, or rebuild connector geometry; keyboard focus may reveal nodes. Preserve the authored routed topology, explicit arrowheads and bridges, fixed detail pane, and independent learned/available/locked/exclusive state markers.
note.summary: Skill progression is immediate, bankable, and hover-stable

note.details: Pointer hover must never change skill selection, the detail pane, focus, scroll, navigation, or connector geometry; only click/controller focus selects a node, and tree nodes have no tooltips because the fixed detail pane owns descriptions. Learning commits immediately and updates the open tree plus level/points/Moltshards chips in place without a redundant success line. Reset spends one Moltshard after one yes/no confirmation, clears the whole tree, and refunds all earned points. Combat activations live in the shared Abilities popover; abilities that discard from hand select the full live hand cards, while discard recovery opens the full-card discard pile. Cache immutable authored skill order and connector obstacle data to avoid first-open and learn stalls.
note.summary: Skill-tree interaction is click-driven, immediate, and zone-preserving

note.details: Manual ability activation is legal only from idle player-turn combat: no selected card, action-mode choice, drag, animation, pending Umbra commit, or existing skill-card selection. Otherwise a saved skill commit can be overwritten later by a stale card preview. Source-zone UI must also translate display order back to the engine's source order; discard piles render newest-first, so Encore buttons bind the reversed source index rather than their displayed index. Full-card hand choices use focusable wrappers with explicit Accept, Cancel, directional navigation, and focus restoration because CardWidget itself is intentionally mouse-only.
note.summary: Combat skill card choices must guard previews and map displayed pile indices

note.details: Card selection wrappers are assembled before CardWidget enters the scene tree. Parent-side recursive mouse-filter changes made before add_child are not sufficient because CardWidget._ready runs afterward. CardWidget must derive mouse_filter from its configured interactive flag in both _ready and later configuration; callers that need nested tooltip hover must pass interactive=true explicitly, while wrapper-owned full-card choices pass false so the wrapper receives the click.
note.summary: CardWidget interaction mode must survive tree entry

note.details: For in-hand skill targeting, lay the prompt out above hand_scroll after the hand is rebuilt instead of using fixed bottom offsets; fixed offsets covered card headers across aspect ratios. For discard-pile targeting, the transparent Button wrapper must draw normal/hover/pressed/focus frames and have explicit focus neighbors to the close action, because CardWidget itself does not own focus.
note.summary: Card-selection prompts are positioned from the live hand boundary, and full-card discard choices require explicit focus frames.

note.details: Use fit-to-view and responsive reflow. The complete tree topology and selected ability rule/action must remain visible; compact layouts may rely on highlighted graph connections instead of redundant prerequisite prose. Enforced by spec/game_ui_rubric.md and tests/test_game_ui_rubric_inventory.py.
note.summary: Player-facing horizontal scrollbars are banned, and skill trees must have no scrollbars on any sub-surface.

note.details: Abilities, relics, equipment, keywords, statuses, resources, and future icon-bearing families may reuse an icon only for the exact same concept. Different concepts may not share a resource path, byte-identical copy, recolor, badge overlay, or generic stand-in. Enforced by spec/icon_identity_policy.md and tests/test_icon_identity_policy.py.
note.summary: Every distinct player-facing icon-bearing concept must own a unique purpose-built icon.

note.details: A unique registry can still be bypassed when RunScene or another consumer locally maps multiple named actions to one generic key, uses a procedural substitute, or falls back to a direct asset path. Keep card/enemy action types and grimoire topic keys centrally inventoried, allow only explicit exact-concept aliases, and assert the real consumers resolve through ActionIconLibrary.
note.summary: Icon identity tests must audit consumers, not only asset inventories

note.details: Pointer hover must never change skill selection, detail, focus, scroll, navigation, or connector geometry; only click/controller focus selects a node, and the no-scroll tree uses large medallions whose unique icons fill most of each face. Learning commits immediately without redundant success copy; whole-tree reset spends one Moltshard after one confirmation and refunds every earned point. Combat uses a labeled Abilities launcher with ready/owned counts and real owned-icon previews (compact below 1100 logical pixels), opening a fixed 800x492, ten-icons-per-page panel with complete two-line names and bounded descriptions. Only manual abilities show an action button. Hand discard and discard recovery select full cards in their source zones, then reuse normal discard/draw card-proxy motion and reduced-motion timing. Cache immutable authored order and connector obstacles to avoid first-open and learn stalls.
note.summary: Skill-tree interaction is click-driven, immediate, icon-led, and zone-preserving

Feeding that projected state directly to CombatBoardView makes _build_visible_units drop the enemy. Keep projected position/status information, restore committed hp/block/stoneskin and missing committed enemies for display, and derive cumulative damage_preview from committed to projected state so empty bars and lethal markers remain visible.

note.details: When a finished card goes to discard, temporarily hold that card out while applying its relic rewards, restore it afterward, and safe-cap default relic draw rewards to the real draw+discard supply. Otherwise draw-trigger relics can self-loop or turn upside into accidental Fatigue damage.
note.summary: Card-play relic draws must not redraw the card that triggered them or create Fatigue.

note.details: Common relics should be easy-to-trigger synergy nudges; rare and epic relics demand narrower or accumulated setup for larger engine payoffs; legendary relics should create run-defining turns only after mythic-level conditions. Avoid unconditional primary attack, health, block, or opening-resource boosts as the obvious picks.
note.summary: Relic rarity is a conditional-power ladder, not a flat efficiency ladder.

note.details: Post-combat reward presentation uses one darkened stage stack: a reusable frayed raster instruction banner with restrained runtime text, exactly three centered card choices, then a compact Skip & Recover button with heal and HP projection. Relic rewards reuse the banner-and-centered-offer composition. Reward fixtures must default to the production three-card offer, never a hand-authored fourth card.
note.summary: Reward offers use a centered ruined raster banner and subordinate Recover

At normal motion, update every display frame; start at impact size, reach a 58 px outward apex around 34% of the 0.84 s lifetime, then drift down while shrinking and lingering. Damage peaks at 60 px, short effects at 48 px, then both shrink along the continuous 0.96 s rise-and-fall arc; hold the peak through 0.32 progress to avoid stepped shrink. Compound effects keep 0.13 s pop-pop-pop staggering, while reduced motion remains a fixed local stack.
note.summary: Combat popups begin close on the target's right side

note.details: For one card-play or status event, evaluate qualifying relic conditions from a shared post-action/post-intensity snapshot before applying same-event rewards, so acquisition order cannot create conditions. Relic card-play rewards earned off the player turn or while player_turn_ending is true accumulate in pending_relic_card_plays and transfer exactly once in prepare_next_player_turn.

Dense hands may tighten idle overlap to a 36 px exposed logical strip so every card remains selectable at 1280x800 and 125% UI scale; reduced motion applies the final pose immediately.

note.details: Until the user explicitly requests a dedicated resolution-focused pass, player-facing UI tasks should capture and inspect only 1920x1080 at 100% UI scale.
